title: Autonomous Firefighting Drone Using ROS, YOLOv8, and ArduPilot with Intelligent Fire-Extinguishing Ball Deployment in Simulated Environments
authors: Kalyani Ghuge; Swapnil Jadhav; Yadhni Kharkar; Prasad Koshatwar; Chaitanya Luniya; Harshada Ghanwat
abstract: This paper presents an autonomous firefighting UAV that integrates ROS2, AirSim, ArduPilot, and a YOLOv8n-based detector to identify fire, smoke, and human victims and deliver fire-extinguishing balls. We quantify system performance across simulation and real-world trials (30 missions): detection mAP@0.5 = 0.925 (avg), end-to-end response time = 58.3 ± 14.2 s, payload delivery accuracy = 0.35 ± 0.18 m, and overall mission success = 80%. Ablation experiments show YOLOv8n provides a favorable tradeoff between inference latency (3.5 ms/frame after TensorRT) and detection accuracy compared to baselines. We discuss failure modes (wind, heavy smoke), statistical significance of results, and practical considerations for field deployment.

title: Research on neural reinforcement learning-based non-inverse kinematics robotic arm control system
authors: Yue Fang; Shizhuo Zhang; Wei Liu
venue: International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Neural Networks (AANN)
abstract: Existing robotic arm control systems usually rely on artificial inverse kinematics modeling to solve, but due to the complexity of the robotic arm, this method is often expensive, particularly when the structure of the robotic arm changes, requiring it to be remodeled and solved again, making it too complex. This paper proposes a neural reinforcement learning-based inverse kinematics robotic arm control system, which only needs to model the forward kinematics of the robotic arm in the virtual simulation environment to JIT generate self-supervised training data to train the neural network, and the network can be used to control any size of hardware robotic arm after the network training converges, as long as its joint arm length ratio is the same as the ratio of training. Experiments show that we can complete this task with a small neural network, and low latency inference servo angle parameters under $150 Jetson Nano, in virtual simulation testing, our control accuracy reaches 97%, while in hardware testing, the accuracy of the camera and servo is reduced, but the control is still effective in the general range. Therefore, this inspires us to study the future research on servo angle nonlinear error correction and the end position control technology under the controlled environment.

title: Real-Time Wound Edge Detection with YOLOv8 for Robotic Suturing in Resource-Constrained Settings
authors: Mostafa AbdelAziz; Zahy Y. Elgendy
abstract: Accurate wound edge detection is a critical step in robotic suturing, especially in settings with limited resources where automation can enhance surgical precision and efficiency. This study presents a real-time computer vision pipeline leveraging the YOLOv8n-seg model to detect and segment wound edges in diverse surgical conditions. The pipeline integrates post-processing techniques, including contour extraction and Ramer-Douglas-Peucker smoothing, to generate precise trajectories suitable for robotic path planning. Trained on a dataset of 2,271 wound images, the model achieved high performance, with mean Average Precision scores ([email protected]) of 0.966 for object detection and 0.961 for segmentation masks, along with high precision and recall. Deployment on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano demonstrated near real-time inference speeds (∼260 ms per image), making the system suitable for interactive robotic applications. This work underscores the feasibility of integrating lightweight, accurate computer vision models into robotic surgical workflows in resource-constrained environments, paving the way for broader adoption of robotic suturing technology. The system specifically responds to infrastructural and workforce constraints common in sub-Saharan Africa. Its standalone, self-contained design eliminates the need for cloud-based processing or expensive server hardware, making its real-time efficiency suitable for rural and under-resourced hospitals. The system design aligns with Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) principles by focusing on usability, autonomy, and contextual relevance for African healthcare environments.

title: A Multi-Modal AI Framework for Autonomous Agricultural Navigation and Coverage Planning using Semantic Costmaps and Drone-based Land Segmentation
authors: R.S.Rajkumar; R.Ram Prakash; J.Akil Prabhu; R.S.Mohana; B. Preetha; S.K.Nivetha
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
abstract: Contemporary autonomous agricultural vehicles suffer from two persistent limitations: binary obstacle occupancy reasoning that cannot distinguish between a proximate human and a distant weed, and uniform terrain treatment that fails to recognise agronomically restricted zones. This paper presents AI agricultural robot that resolves both limitations through three integrated contributions deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin platform. First, a priority-weighted costmap layer driven by a custom YOLOv8 model trained on eleven farm-specific obstacle classes assigns semantically graded, confidence- and proximity-modulated costs to detected objects, enabling proportional navigation responses. Second, AgroCpp, a boustrophedon coverage path planner implemented in C++ under ROS 2 Nav2, generates optimised crop-row-aligned paths and performs real-time obstacle-reactive replanning through a six-state execution automaton without full mission restart. Third, a YOLOv8-seg instance segmentation pipeline processes drone-view imagery across twelve agronomic land-use classes, collapses outputs into three navigation zones, and publishes cost values directly to a dedicated Nav2 costmap layer, coupling aerial agronomic awareness to ground-vehicle path planning. The multi-sensor hardware stack integrates a Livox Mid-70 solid-state LiDAR, ZED 2i stereo camera, Sony IMX477 global-shutter camera, and H-RTK F9P RTK-GNSS receiver for sensor-fusion-based traversability estimation. Performance targets including mAP@0.5 ≥ 0.70 for obstacle detection, mIoU ≥ 0.65 for land segmentation, path generation within 100 ms, and 15 ms TensorRT inference latency are formally defined and experimentally evaluated. The proposed multisensory fusion technology along with precision agricultural method will be very useful for modern agricultural needs

title: Performance Evaluation of Recent Object Detection Models for Traffic Safety Applications on Edge
authors: Anilcan Bulut; Fatmanur Ozdemir; Yavuz Selim Bostanci; Müjdat Soytürk
venue: International Conference on Image Processing and Machine Vision (IPMV)
abstract: Real-time objection detection is becoming more important and critical in all application areas, including Smart Transport and Smart City. From safety/security to resource efficiency, real-time image processing approaches are used more than ever. On the other hand, low-latency requirements and available resources present challenges. Edge computing integrated with cloud computing minimizes communication delays but requires efficient use of resources due to its limited resources. For example, although deep learning-based object detection methods give very accurate and reliable results, they require high computational power. This overhead reveals a need to implement deep learning models with less complex architectures for edge deployment. In this paper, the performance of evolving deep learning models with their lightweight versions such as YOLOv5-Nano, YOLOX-Nano, YOLOX-Tiny, YOLOv6-Nano, YOLOv6-Tiny, and YOLOv7-Tiny are evaluated on a commercially available edge device. The results show that YOLOv5-Nano and YOLOv6-Nano with their TensorRT versions can provide real-time applicability in approximately 35 milliseconds of inference time. It is also observed that YOLOv6-Tiny gives the highest average precision while YOLOv5-Nano gives the lowest energy consumption when compared to other models.

title: IF-DQN: A Network-Aware Autonomous Agent-Driven Framework for AI Inference Task Offloading
authors: Xianhui Liu; Junlong Zhao; Chenglin Zhu; D M Yu; Weidong Zhao
venue: KSII Transactions on Internet and Information Systems
abstract: The growing integration of AI and the Industrial Internet has intensified the need for rapid deployment of AI inference services at the edge.However, existing task offloading approaches often fail to address framework heterogeneity, computational load, and latency sensitivity, resulting in inefficient resource utilization and high delays.To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes IF-DQN, a network-aware, autonomous agent-driven task offloading framework for Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) scenarios.In IF-DQN, edge inference nodes are modeled as agents that continuously perceive bandwidth, latency, and resource load, while deep reinforcement learning (DQN) is employed to autonomously learn cross-layer offloading strategies, enabling dynamic task allocation and resource coordination across cloud-edge-end layers.An inference framework matching mechanism is further incorporated to ensure compatibility between tasks and runtime environments, enhancing stability and utilization.Experimental results on the self-developed MaaSim simulation platform show that IF-DQN achieves rapid convergence, higher cumulative rewards, reduced inference latency, improved resource utilization, and nearly 100% task completion rates under diverse conditions.These findings highlight IF-DQN as an effective and robust solution for embodied AI in collaborative cloud-edge-end environments.

title: An Improved MPANet-Based Method for Autonomous Identification of Construction Disturbance Areas in Transmission Line Projects
authors: Zhipeng Shang; Mingliang Zhao; Wei Yong; Jing Peng; W M Liu; Zhao Xushan
venue: International Conference on Smart Grid and Artificial Intelligence (SGAI)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved MPANet model for the autonomous identification of construction disturbance areas and precise measurement of construction road lengths in transmission line projects. Through technological innovations including multi-scale feature extraction, enhanced spatial attention mechanisms, few-shot learning optimization, and imaging-condition-based data augmentation, the model effectively addresses challenges in transmission line construction monitoring, such as difficulties in multi-source data fusion, insufficient accuracy in identifying disturbance areas, scarcity of annotated data, and complex, variable construction scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved MPANet model achieves an mAP of 89.3% and an IoU of 82.5% in the task of detecting construction disturbances for transmission lines, representing improvements of 16.2% and 9.3%, respectively, over the traditional YOLOv5 model. Furthermore, it achieves a real-time inference speed of 25 FPS on the Jetson AGX Xavier edge device. Compared to traditional manual inspection methods, this model improves the efficiency of disturbance area detection by more than fivefold and enhances detection accuracy by over 40%, providing an intelligent and efficient technical solution for construction safety management and control in transmission line projects.

title: Edge Computing Approach to AI-Based Gesture for Human–Robot Interaction and Control
authors: Nikola Ivačko; Ivan S Ciric; Miloš Simonović
abstract: This paper presents an edge-deployable vision-based framework for human–robot interaction using a xArm collaborative robot and a single RGB camera mounted on the robot wrist, and lightweight AI-based perception modules. The system enables intuitive, contact-free control by combining hand understanding and object detection within a unified perception–decision–control pipeline. Hand landmarks are extracted using MediaPipe Hands, from which continuous hand trajectories, static gestures, and dynamic gestures are derived. Task objects are detected using a YOLO-based model, and both hand and object observations are mapped into the robot workspace using ArUco-based planar calibration. To ensure stable robot motion, the hand control signal is smoothed using low-pass and Kalman filtering, while dynamic gestures such as waving are recognized using a lightweight LSTM classifier. The complete pipeline runs locally on edge hardware, specifically NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo AI accelerator. Experimental evaluation includes trajectory stability, gesture recognition reliability, and runtime performance on both platforms. Results show that filtering significantly reduces hand-tracking jitter, gesture recognition provides stable command states for control, and both edge devices support real-time operation, with Jetson achieving consistently lower runtime than Raspberry Pi. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of low-cost edge AI solutions for responsive and practical human–robot interaction in collaborative industrial environments.

title: Toward End-to-End Event-Driven Systems: A Hardware-Oriented Hierarchical Spiking Predictive Coding Framework for On-Device Learning
authors: Jung-Gyun Kim; Byung‐Geun Lee
abstract: Integrating on-device learning into autonomous systems requires neural network frameworks that achieve both high energy efficiency and low latency. While spiking neural networks (SNNs) provide a promising event-driven paradigm, implementing hardware-efficient learning remains a challenge due to the computational overhead of error signaling and global gradients. This paper introduces a hardware-oriented hierarchical spiking predictive coding (SPC) framework designed for end-to-end event-driven systems. The proposed architecture implements an implicit prediction error encoding mechanism through local lateral and supervisory feedback connections, eliminating the need for dedicated error-storage memory or complex inter-layer error communication. The entire framework is structured and parameterized for physical implementation, utilizing digital-aligned simulations and arithmetic operations. We evaluate the system on neuromorphic datasets using a fixed 1 ms temporal resolution to mirror real-time hardware constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the SPC framework can effectively identify stimuli from transient event streams, achieving stable on-device learning. Our work provides a practical path toward deploying low-power, scalable hierarchical spiking networks in resource-constrained environments.

title: Design of autonomous obstacle avoidance system for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles based on MID-360 LiDAR
authors: Hongyu Fan
venue: International Symposium on Sensors, Mechatronics, and Automation System (ISSMAS)
abstract: Autonomous navigation of multi-rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in complex low-altitude environments remains challenging due to severe onboard computational constraints, sensor blind spots, and unpredictable dynamic obstacles. This paper presents a lightweight, integrated autonomous obstacle avoidance system for quadrotors utilizing a MID-360 solid-state LiDAR. To achieve robust state estimation, FAST-LIO2 is employed as a high-frequency odometry backend. For dynamic environments, an Unscented Kalman Filter(UKF) integrated with a Constant Turn Rate and Velocity (CTRV) motion model is proposed to detect, track, and predict the non-linear trajectories of moving obstacles in real time. For motion planning, an Euclidean Signed Distance Field (ESDF)-free gradient-based local planner is developed, which incorporates an adaptive safety inflation layer tailored specifically to compensate for the vertical field-of-view (FOV) blind zones of the MID-360 sensor during aggressive maneuvers. The entire system is deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano onboard compute platform. Extensive simulations and real-world flight tests demonstrate that the proposed system achieves ultra-low latency trajectory re-planning (within 10ms) and ensures robust collision-free flight against both static and dynamic hazards, exhibiting superior execution efficiency and safety.

title: Fail-Closed, On-Device Agentic Orchestration for Mobile Operating Systems: Design, Implementation, and Real-Hardware Validation on Android
authors: Ilan Sezhiyan Jayaraman
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Smartphones have accumulated capability faster than they have accumulated usability: using any of it still requires knowing which app holds a function, navigating that app’s interface, and manually carrying state between apps for any task spanning more than one. We present AgentOS, an intent-driven Android layer that replaces this app-mediated interaction model with a single natural-language surface backed by a six-layer orchestration architecture spanning UI, orchestration engine, on-device AI run-time, native tool capabilities, context storage, and device provisioning. AgentOS contributes two central mechanisms. Fail-closed capability registration excludes a native tool from a language-model planner’s schema entirely, before inference, when the tool’s backing data-source confidence falls below a threshold τ — preventing an unreliable call from ever being offered to the model, rather than validating or blocking it after generation. Hardware-capability-aware routing uses a declarative per-device profile, consumed identically by both the AI runtime and the native capability layer at initialization, to decouple orchestration logic from any single device’s sensor, camera, and compute characteristics. A supporting sensor-context safety-escalation mechanism governs dispatch-time authorization for consequential actions. We evaluate AgentOS end-to-end on a real Samsung Galaxy F34 device provisioned under Android’s Device-Owner model — not emulation or scripted traces — across seventeen native tool executors spanning telephony, messaging, calendar, camera, location, media, fitness, and notifications. Thirteen of seventeen executors pass end-to-end; every remaining failure is root-caused to a specific external cause rather than left unexplained. The fast-classified path meets its sub-two-second latency budget; an LLM-escalation path, evaluated across five candidate on-device models, does not, by a disclosed and substantial margin. We situate both central mechanisms against the closest available prior art — including concurrent industry work on pre-inference tool-schema gating — and report real engineering failures, root causes, and open limitations alongside the results that favor the system.

title: A Three-Stage On-Device Machine Learning Pipeline for Service-Aware Power Optimization in 5G User Equipment
authors: Jong-Phil Lee; Boyoung Kim
abstract: Advancements in next-generation wireless communication technologies, such as 5G, have enabled the utilization of Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) and Enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) resources. To enhance user-perceived performance, or Quality of Experience (QoE), it is essential to appropriately allocate network resources to applications based on their specific requirements. Consequently, there is a growing necessity for intelligent resource management at the User Equipment (UE) level. This study proposes a three-stage on-device ML pipeline for service-aware power optimization in 5G UE. The pipeline consists of: (1) a Traffic Classifier (XGBoost) that performs real-time binary classification of RT/NRT traffic; (2) a NO-DATA Predictor (Student-LogReg with Knowledge Distillation) that forecasts traffic-idle intervals in NRT sessions; and (3) a Finite State Machine (FSM) Controller that selectively suspends classifier inference during predicted NO-DATA periods. The FSM Controller suspends classifier operation at P(NO-DATA) ≥ 0.80 for two consecutive slots and resumes at P(NO-DATA) < 0.60, enabling recovery within one slot. Experimental evaluations on real-world KT 5G SA network traffic data demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a 61.42% reduction in classifier inference calls while maintaining a QoE error rate of 0.26% and zero RECLASSIFY events, confirming that the Predictor's DATA Recall of 98.35% effectively serves as a safety net against classifier misclassification. This approach provides a practical solution for implementing application-aware, energy-efficient network management in resource-constrained on-device environments. To validate generalizability beyond simulation, the pipeline was installed on a custom-built Android measurement application and field-tested on seven Samsung Galaxy device models across six countries (Korea, Japan, Australia, Mexico, Brazil, and the United Kingdom) on commercial networks, yielding 28 measurement sessions with RECLASSIFY = 0 in all cases. Real-world field measurements show reduction rates ranging from 19.6% to 60.4%, with NRT applications (YouTube, Netflix) achieving a mean of 46.1% compared to 33.2% for RT applications (YouTube Live, Zoom), confirming a 12.9 pp service-type gap consistent with the simulation results.

title: SELIX: An Autonomous Unmanned Ground Vehicle for Urban Search and Rescue via Thermal–Visible Fusion and Edge SLAM
authors: أ.د. سمير سليمان الجمل
venue: Stardom doğa ve mühendislik çalışmaları dergisi.
abstract: Search and rescue (SAR) operations in post-disaster rubble environments face critical challenges from structural instability, low visibility, toxic gas accumulation, and degraded communications, while existing teleoperated unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) suffer from high operator fatigue, high latency, and single-modal sensor failure under smoke or zero-light conditions. The problem addressed by this research is the design of an autonomous UGV capable of reliable victim detection and safe navigation in such hazardous, GPS-denied environments. A design-science and experimental engineering methodology was adopted to develop the proposed platform, SELIX, which integrates a hierarchical dual-processing architecture combining an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano for high-level perception and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) with an STM32 microcontroller for low-level real-time actuation. Data were collected from an integrated sensing suite comprising RGB and long-wave-infrared thermal cameras, a 2D LiDAR, an inertial measurement unit (IMU), ultrasonic sensors, and a gas-sensor array, together with an annotated image dataset of 2,500 samples (split 70% training, 15% validation, 15% testing) built by merging open-source data with additional site-representative images. Detection was performed using an anchor-free, TensorRT-optimized YOLOv8 model trained on fused thermal-visible imagery; localization relied on an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) fusing wheel odometry, IMU, and LiDAR readings; and navigation combined global A∗ path planning with a hazard-aware Dynamic Window Approach informed by real-time gas telemetry. System performance was evaluated using precision, recall, mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5), inference latency, localization drift, and mission success rate across 50 integrated search-and-rescue trials. Results show that the thermal-visible YOLOv8 pipeline achieved 92.4% precision and 91.2% mAP@0.5 at 28 ms inference latency, improving detection success by 15% over RGB-only imagery under low-light conditions; the EKF-SLAM engine maintained 93% localization accuracy and kept trajectory drift below 0.24 m on severe rubble terrain; and the integrated platform achieved an 88% overall mission success rate with an average task completion time of 4.5 minutes. These findings position SELIX as a scalable, high-throughput solution for real-time victim localization and hazard assessment in disaster response missions.

title: Implementation of Sensor-Fused Semi-Autonomous Rover for Safe Rescue Mission and Terrain Mapping
authors: Sivaramakrishnan R; M. Lakshmi Keerthana; Sriram A; R. Prithiviraj
venue: IEEE International Conference on Recent Advances in Computing and Systems (REACS)
abstract: Rescue operations in hazardous environments demand rapid situational awareness, reliable communication, and autonomous mobility to reduce risks for both victims and responders. This paper presents the design and evaluation of the Semi-Autonomous Rescue Rover System (SARRS), a unified platform integrating multi-sensor fusion, real-time data analysis, and continuous wireless communication to support disaster response teams. The rover employs proximity, thermal, motion, environmental hazard, and positioning sensors to autonomously navigate challenging terrains, detect human presence, and monitor critical environmental conditions while transmitting live data to remote operators. An embedded AI-assisted vision module performs on-device detection with low latency, eliminating dependence on external processing. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high detection accuracy, efficient navigation coverage, and rapid alert delivery, significantly improving mission efficiency and safety. SARRS provides a scalable, low-cost methodology for deploying semi-autonomous systems in real-world rescue scenarios, reducing operational risks and enhancing outcomes in time-sensitive missions.

title: Neural Computing-Driven Signal Processing Frameworks for IoT-Enabled AR/VR and Robotic Systems: A VLSI-Centric Perspective
venue: Journal of VLSI Circuits and Systems
abstract: The article presents a very large-scale integration (VLSI)-based neural signal processing system that is meant to provide high-performance, low-latency, and energy-efficient computations to realize next-generation IoT-enabled augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR) and robotics.The architecture suggested combines the hardware/software co-design, neural model compression, and scalable VLSI implementation to facilitate real-time on-device intelligence.Fundamentally, the architecture has an adaptive multistage pipeline that integrates multimodal sensor data vision, motion, and environmental streams via a hybrid neural signal processing stack composed of convolutional, recurrent, and spiking neural modules.In contrast to traditional DSP or entirely algorithmic accelerators, the system is based on VLSI-conscious neural mapping, dataflow scheduling, and precision-adaptive arithmetic to reduce the computation latency and power consumption with a rigid set of edge resources.Designed on a reconfigurable FPGA-VLSI platform, the design has shown significant benefits in a variety of AR/VR and robotic metrics with the lowest system latency, throughput, and energy consumption of up to 3.2×, 2.7×, and 58%, respectively, over initial DSP and classical processing designs.These findings affirm that the framework is a single, extensible platform of real-time signal-driven intelligence, which can be developed to enhance immersive, autonomous, and edge-sensitive computing platforms in smart robotics, wearable systems, and cyber-physical environments.

title: Re-Parameterized Real-Time Stereo Matching Network Based on Mixed Cost Volumes Toward Autonomous Driving
authors: Bowen Yao; Wei Wei; Jinhao Huang; Bifa Liang; Jun Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: 3D perception is an essential capability of autonomous vehicles. Most state-of-the-art stereo matching networks pursue higher prediction accuracy at the cost of the inference speed. However, high demand on computational resource pushes the cost of hardware, hindering practical applications of stereo matching. In this paper, we propose RMCNet, a novel re-parameterized coarse-to-fine network for stereo matching. RMCNet achieves real time on edge devices while outputs accurate disparity maps. To reduce the computing complexity of 3D convolution in cost aggregation, we propose Mixed Cost Volumes that consist of 4D and 3D cost volumes, enabling efficient optimization of the initial disparity map for real-time inference. An Efficient Feature Matching module is proposed to provide absolute disparity candidates for 3D cost volume. To increase the reliability of 4D and 3D cost volumes, we propose a simple but efficient 3D cost aggregation module and a pyramid 2D cost aggregation module for the aggregation of Mixed Cost Volumes. Moreover, we propose a Re-parameterized Channel Sensing module and a Re-parameterized Disparity-Aware module to replace 2D and 3D convolutional blocks with residual connections. Being evaluated on KITTI 2012 and KITTI 2015, the comprehensive performance of the proposed network is improved by the re-parameterization approach. Outstanding trade-off between accuracy and speed on edge devices over existing SOTA works is achieved. With fast average inference speed on NVIDIA Jetson Nano of 33.74 FPS, the accuracy in terms of 3px-all on KITTI 2012 test set and D1-all on KITTI 2015 test set are 3.01% and 3.41%, respectively.

title: XGate-Net: Bidirectional Cross-Task Gating Fusion Network for Multi-Task Perception in Autonomous Driving
authors: Sungjun Jang; Minkyoung Kim; Dongjin Jeon; Taegeun Oh

title: A Critical Analysis of Edge-Deployable Vision-Based Assistive Navigation Systems: From Detection Accuracy to Real-World Safety
authors: Hardik Arora; Amit Gupta; Nirbhik Yadav; Aanchal; Puneet
venue: International Conference on Information, Implementation, and Innovation in Technology (I2ITCON)
abstract: As deep learning, edge computing, and wearable sensing technologies have advanced, vision-based assistive navigation systems have evolved rapidly. The performance of these systems in real world safety-critical mobility scenarios has received little attention, despite recent studies showing notable improvements in object detection accuracy and real-time inference on embedded platforms. This review focuses on the trade-offs between detection accuracy, latency, edge deployment feasibility, and human-centered evaluation by critically examining recent studies on vision-based navigation systems for blind and visually impaired individuals. We present a systematic taxonomy that groups systems according to feedback modality, mapping capability, deployment platform, and detection architecture. A quantitative comparative analysis reveals recurring patterns, such as the limited reporting of end-to-end latency and power consumption and the performance degradation of lightweight models in small-object detection. More significantly, we find a substantial evaluation gap: while the majority of studies report algorithmic metrics such as mAP and FPS, very few evaluate navigation safety through longitudinal user studies or objective safety metrics such as collision rates. We suggest a unified four-layer evaluation framework that incorporates algorithmic, system-level, user-level, and safety-level metrics in order to overcome this limitation. Lastly, we present a systematic research roadmap for improving assistive navigation systems by enhancing edge efficiency, reliability, and real-world validation. The goal of this review is to reorient the field toward deployable, user-centered, and safety-aware assistive technologies.

title: Cognitive Edge Intelligence for Cooperative Driving Safety: A Digital Shadow Framework in Industry 5.0
authors: Sana Saleh; Alireza Jolfaei; Muhammad Huzaifa Tariq
abstract: Industry 5.0 envisions a human-centric, cognitively aware transportation ecosystem emphasizing resilience, personalization, and sustainable human-machine collaboration. This paper proposes a unified cognitive edge intelligence framework that transforms individual driving behavior into collective, predictive safety intelligence. The framework integrates Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML), cooperative perception, and human-in-the-loop augmented intelligence for real-time driver behavior understanding at the network edge. Unlike traditional cloud-centric or reactive systems, our approach employs lightweight, optimized TinyML models on in-vehicle edge units to infer behavioral states, normal, slow, and aggressive, directly from inertial sensor streams with minimal latency. This cognitive state is shared via an Internet of Vehicles (IoV) layer, enabling collective risk anticipation beyond line-of-sight. A digital shadow aggregates behavioral insights from connected vehicles to support long-term trend analysis and statistical anomaly detection, completing a closed-loop intelligence cycle from edge inference to strategic fleet oversight. The framework is experimentally validated across multiple dimensions. Real-world driving data demonstrates the system's efficacy, achieving 97.75% test accuracy and 95.7% accuracy on a separate real-world deployment dataset, with an ultralight model size of 0.03 MB and a per-inference latency of 0.35 ms. The cooperative Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) mechanism achieves a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) exceeding 96.5% with end-to-end latency below 2 ms across highway traffic densities, while the digital shadow enables behavioral trend monitoring and statistical anomaly detection. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework delivers both immediate roadside safety and long-term system-wide resilience for next-generation transportation systems.

title: Deep Learning-Enhanced Edge-AI Architecture for Autonomous Drone-based Traffic Flow Prediction and Congestion Management
authors: P Yashini; R. Renugadevi; Berlin Magthalin R
venue: International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
abstract: The rapid growth of urban populations has intensified traffic congestion, making real-time monitoring and predictive management essential for smart city infrastructure. This paper proposes a deep learning-driven Edge-AI framework deployed on autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to perform real-time traffic analysis, incident detection, and congestion prediction in dynamic urban environments. The system integrates high-resolution aerial video capture with on-board deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures optimized for edge inference, eliminating reliance on constant cloud connectivity. A multi-stage processing pipeline enables vehicle detection, trajectory extraction, and traffic flow estimation directly on the UAV, followed by edge-to-edge coordination between drones for large-scale coverage. Experiments conducted on publicly available drone-traffic datasets, enhanced with custom aerial recordings, demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves over 94% detection accuracy with sub second inference latency, while significantly reducing bandwidth usage compared to cloud-based methods. The framework’s adaptability to varying traffic densities and lighting conditions highlights its potential for deployment in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), urban planning, and emergency response. This work contributes a scalable, privacy-preserving, and latency-optimized solution for next-generation traffic management in smart cities.

title: An Onboard Integrated Perception and Control Framework for Autonomous Quadrotor UAV Perching on Markerless Hurdles
authors: Donghyun Kim; Dong Eui Chang
abstract: This paper presents an onboard, markerless perching system for a quadrotor UAV, validated in outdoor flight experiments, to reduce hovering energy during long-endurance unmanned missions. Existing autonomous landing research predominantly focuses on planar surfaces, cooperative environments with visual markers, or specialized hardware, limiting scalability to scenarios requiring detection and perching on thin rod-like targets in uncooperative outdoor settings. This study proposes a markerless perching system for autonomously perching a drone on a hurdle’s horizontal bar. The system employs a single-axis gimbal camera, altitude LiDAR, and ToF sensor, integrating perception, post-processing, and control. On the perception side, we augment a YOLOv12n-based segmentation model with a high-resolution P2 pathway for small-object detection and apply module compression for real-time inference on edge devices. Robustness is improved by jointly utilizing the full hurdle and horizontal bar while constructing negative samples to suppress false positives. On the control side, a state machine controller leverages centroid coordinates, orientation, and distance measurements to achieve a stable long-range approach and precise close-range alignment. Experiments on a Jetson Orin NX-based system demonstrate successful perching in all six outdoor flight tests. Ablation studies quantitatively analyze each component’s contribution to perching success rate and completion time. This research validates perching technology’s practical applicability through outdoor markerless perching on thin 3D structures.

title: Evaluation of Computer Vision-Driven Autonomous Water Landing of Amphibious UAVs Using YOLOv8 and MATLAB
authors: E Kannan; Surendar Ganesan; Balasubramanian Esakki; Ch. Nirmal Prabhath
venue: International Conference on Communications and Signal Processing (ICCSP)
abstract: Traditional sensors, such as GPS, barometric, and ultrasonic sensors, have limitations in accurately reflecting and dynamically capturing data from water surfaces, particularly during the unsafe landing of a UAV at precise locations. To overcome these limitations, a computer vision-driven landing zone detection framework using a YOLOv8 deep learning model is being trained on a custom dataset and imported within a MATLAB simulation environment. In this research, a MATLAB-based simulation architecture for identifying safe water landing zones in a camera-based virtual environment is designed. The custom datasets are annotated and trained using the YOLOv8 architecture with the best.pt weights are deployed in MATLAB for real-time inference. In the MATLAB environment, the virtual camera sensor processes input video streams, providing real-time object detection and classification and enabling the identification of safe landing zones over the water body under varying environmental conditions, including dynamic water and lighting conditions. The proposed system achieves high detection accuracy in safe-zone landing detection and demonstrates the effectiveness of the computer vision-based autonomous water-landing system for amphibious UAVs. The results show that the planned methods are suitable for applications, such as environmental monitoring, search and rescue, and maritime surveillance operations involving amphibious UAVs. Future work will focus on improving simulation-based validation for real-time embedded hardware deployment using an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, integrating an RGB camera and mmWave radar.

title: Bridging the camera gap: evaluating AI-based cross-sensor domain shift in weed detection on the amiga robotic platform
authors: Mohamed Abdallah Salem; Ahmed Harb Rabia
venue: Autonomous Air and Ground Sensing Systems for Agricultural Optimization and Phenotyping
abstract: Reliable weed detection on agricultural robots depends not only on model architecture but also on the imaging sensor used at deployment. This paper examines cross-sensor domain shift for weed detection on the Amiga robotic platform by training detectors on high-resolution DSLR imagery and evaluating them on several simulated embedded-camera domains. A dataset of 100 Canon DSLR images was annotated in YOLO format and reused consistently across all domains to isolate the effect of sensor characteristics from label variation. Camera-specific image formation was approximated using a transformation pipeline that combines resolution downsampling, Gaussian sensor noise, optical blur, spectral modification for infrared behavior, and compression artifacts. Four YOLO-based detector configurations were evaluated in single-class and multi-class settings, with both scratch and pretrained initialization. Performance was assessed using mAP50, mAP50–95, precision, recall, and inference latency. The results demonstrate substantial degradation under cross-sensor shift, with the largest losses observed in the infrared domain. Multi-class models were more sensitive to this shift and showed reductions approaching 40–50% in the most difficult conditions, whereas single-class models remained comparatively stable. Among the evaluated configurations, YOLOV12SP achieved the strongest overall accuracy, while YOLOV12SS provided the most favorable speed–performance trade-off for edge deployment. The analysis also indicates that a small subset of sensors can mildly improve performance relative to the DSLR baseline, suggesting limited feature alignment between some transformed domains and the learned representations. These findings highlight the importance of camera-aware evaluation when transferring weed detection systems from controlled training imagery to practical robotic sensing platforms.

title: Karana: A Post-Quantum Secure AI Surveillance System for Autonomous Multimodal Threat Detection
authors: Satyander Kaushik; Ravneet Kaur
venue: International Conference on Innovations and Emerging Technologies in AI & Communication Systems (IETACS)
abstract: Karana is a surveillance system driven by artificial intelligence (AI) that can identify threats instantly and react safely in ever-more complicated settings. Designed for industrial facilities, smart cities, and defense zones, Karana integrates edge AI, multimodal sensing, and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) into a single, intelligent platform. Because they rely on manual oversight, cloud inference, and monomodal inputs, traditional surveillance infrastructures are susceptible to cyberphysical breaches, spoofing, and lax reaction times. Even while AI-based systems improve visual analytics, many of them are still only capable of single-sensor streams and lack reliable, on-device decision-making, which makes them useless against threats from autonomous drones, GNSS jamming, and encrypted RF spoofing. By combining radio frequency (RF), infrared (IR), radar, and red-green-blue (RGB) video data, Karana fills in these gaps. An edge AI engine that runs Swin Transformer, You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8), and a suggested quantum-inspired classifier processes these. Rapid, context-aware threat mitigation is made possible by this approach, which also removes reliance on external processing. CRYSTALS-Kyber and Dilithium2, two PQC protocols that comply with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), are used to strengthen security. A policydriven rule engine automatically chooses graded non- lethal actions, including alarm broadcasts, lockdowns, or signal jamming, based on the type and origin of the threat. Karana maintained an average inference latency of 52.9 milliseconds across multimodal inputs and obtained an F1 score of 90.0 when validated with simulation workflows. These findings validate realtime performance in hostile, low-light, and spoofing scenarios. Future stages will include adversarial robustness testing and hardware optimization.

title: AI- and IoT-Based Risk Perception and Safety Warning for Assisted Driving
authors: Ning Wei
abstract: Assisted-driving systems remain constrained by sensor occlusion, adverse weather, and unrealistic assumptions of full vehicle-to-everything (V2X) availability. This paper proposes an AI- and IoT-based risk perception framework integrating context-adaptive multi-head attention fusion of camera, radar, LiDAR, and V2X data, a safety-oriented time-to-collision (TTC) penalty loss, and a V2X-penetration-aware warning mechanism. The model, deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge platform, was evaluated on highD, CARLA, and BDD100K benchmarks using 5-fold cross-validation. The framework achieved 95.8 ± 0.6% risk classification accuracy, a Critical-class F1-score of 0.940, and 43 ms end-to-end latency at 23.1 FPS. Warning performance degraded gracefully from 100% to 94% true-positive rate as V2X penetration fell from 100% to 40%, outperforming the standalone ADAS baseline (87%). The results confirm that adaptive multi-modal fusion with asymmetric loss design enables reliable, real-time hazard warning in mixed-traffic environments.

title: Computer Vision for Real-Time Safety Compliance Monitoring in Machinery Spaces
authors: Goodnews Ogboada Jaja; Daniel Tamunodukobipi
venue: International Journal of Modern Innovations and Knowledge
abstract: Machinery spaces aboard marine vessels, including engine rooms and auxiliary compartments, remain safety-critical environments where manual supervision and periodic inspections can miss time-sensitive non-compliance events. This study develops and evaluates a real-time computer vision framework for automated safety compliance monitoring in marine machinery spaces, with emphasis on personal protective equipment (PPE) detection and context-aware alerting. The approach fine-tunes a YOLOv8 single-stage detector using domain-adapted, augmented open-source industrial safety imagery to approximate vessel-specific conditions such as poor illumination, vibration-induced blur, occlusions, and constrained layouts. The monitoring logic models the machinery space as discrete risk zones and flags violations when human presence is detected without full PPE compliance, enabling spatially localised, time-dependent alerts. Experimental results demonstrate strong detection performance across PPE classes, with precision of 0.84, recall of 0.81, F1-score of 0.82, and mAP@0.5 of 0.85. The model also exhibits stable training behaviour, reaching validation mAP@0.5 of 0.85 after 20 epochs. For edge feasibility, simulation on embedded platforms shows frame-wise inference times clustering between 28.5 ms and 31.5 ms on Jetson Nano, remaining below the 33.3 ms threshold required for 30 FPS real-time operation. Risk-zone analytics further indicate higher violation frequencies around the engine block and compressor unit, supporting targeted safety auditing and intervention planning. Overall, the proposed framework provides a practical pathway for low-latency, onboard safety compliance monitoring aligned with maritime operational constraints and regulatory expectations

title: AI-Embedded Optical Modules With Millisecond-Granularity Power Analysis for Autonomous Metro Transport Network and Field Trial
authors: Xinyu Chen; Liuyan Han; Zixi Liu; Wei He; Xuegang Ou; Dechao Zhang; Han Li
abstract: The rapid expansion of 5G-A/6 G and AI-driven data centers demands robust optical networks with real-time fault detection capabilities. To address this need, we propose an intelligent optical module for edge deployment featuring millisecond-granularity power sampling and AI-driven analytics for high-precision monitoring of optical failures. The system integrates a hardware-software co-design enabling 10 ms resolution with a dual-attentive optic-diagnose network (DAOD-Net), which combines conditional GAN-based data augmentation and a TimeTransformer architecture for enhanced fault classification. Real-time inference for multiple failure modes is achieved, including device failure, fiber break, pigtail detachment, connector loosening, and fiber bend. Field trials in the deployed network demonstrate an overall fault identification accuracy of 92.6% with the consistent >95% precision across all fault categories, outperforming traditional neural network methods by 14.7% in accuracy. This solution is promising for reducing optical fault diagnostic time from hours to seconds, advancing the state-of-the-art in network automation capabilities while providing a scalable framework for proactive maintenance in next-generation 5G-A/6 G and hyperscale data center networks.

title: MT-REN: An Energy-Efficient Metric–Topology-Fusion Reconfigurable End-to-End GVD-NeuroSLAM Accelerator for Autonomous Microrobots
authors: Zixuan Shen; Jian Xiao; Boyi Dong; Zhengzhe Wei; Yulong Tan; Zhigang Wu; Yuanjin Zheng; Chao Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems
abstract: Path exploration, localization, and mapping are fundamental capabilities for autonomous microrobots, which require high energy efficiency and low hardware overhead for long-term edge deployment. However, it remains challenging to simultaneously achieve high energy efficiency, high precision, and low latency on energy-constrained robotic platforms. To address the above challenges, this article proposes a brain-inspired metric–topology-fusion reconfigurable GVD-NeuroSLAM hardware accelerator. At the algorithm level, a metric–topology-fusion GVD-NeuroSLAM algorithm is proposed, where a generalized Voronoi diagram (GVD) provides topology-constrained metric estimation to enhance the precision of NeuroSLAM, while NeuroSLAM provides metric-corrected exploration-direction refinement to achieve efficient exploration. At the architecture level, a reconfigurable end-to-end GVD-NeuroSLAM hardware accelerator, MT-REN, is proposed, which integrates a topology-guided LiDAR point filtering module and a metric-guided continuous attractor neural network (CANN) module to reduce redundant exploration energy consumption while improving SLAM precision. At the microarchitecture level, a fast-convergence CORDIC-based configurable coordinate calculation module and a workload-aware reconfigurable dual-mode processing element (PE) cluster are developed to further enhance energy efficiency, hardware utilization, and computational speed. FPGA implementation results show that the proposed MT-REN achieves significantly higher energy efficiency than conventional visual SLAM (VSLAM) accelerators and higher precision with negligible hardware and latency overhead than the state-of-the-art NeuroSLAM accelerator.

title: Nirbhaya: A Smart Mobile Application for Women Safety
venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
abstract: Women's safety remains a critical societal concern, necessitating intelligent, real-time technological interventions.This paper presents Nirbhaya, a cross-platform mobile application developed using Flutter, designed to provide multi-layered personal safety to women through AI-driven threat detection and automated emergency response.The study investigates the design, development, and integration of three core detection mechanisms: Eye Gesture SOS using Google ML Kit Face Detection, Panic Whisper Detection via a native Android foreground service with continuous speech recognition, and a Danger Prediction Service that evaluates contextual risk factors in real time.The application further integrates a Gemini-powered AI safety chatbot, realtime GPS location sharing, emergency contact management, and cloud-based SOS alert delivery through Firebase and Twilio.Results demonstrate that the multi-modal approach significantly improves detection reliability across foreground and background states.The system achieves seamless switching between detection modes based on app lifecycle, ensuring continuous protection.The study concludes that combining on-device ML inference with cloud-backed emergency dispatch provides a robust, low-latency safety solution suitable for real-world deployment on Android devices.

title: An Autonomous Drone System for Real-Time Object Tracking and Gesture Control Using Edge Computing
authors: Nhu Thanh Vo; Ngoc Tien Hung Ho; Van Loi Cao; Tran Cong Quy Van; The Can Do; Quang Khai Tran
venue: International Conference on Applying New Technology in Green Buildings (ATiGB)
abstract: There is a rapidly growing demand for human-machine interfaces (HMIs) and autonomous navigation capabilities in everyday applications, especially in the field of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Nevertheless, such advanced features of computer vision and image processing algorithms are not yet widely available on standalone devices. In this paper, we propose that there is a lightweight and intelligent drone system that achieves object recognition and tracking as well as hand gesture recognition in real time based on edge computing technology. The integration hardware architecture includes a Pixhawk flight controller and Jetson Nano embedded computer, all of which are mounted on a large carbon fiber frame that guarantees long-lasting as well as stable deployment. Real-time image data provided by a camera module gets processed in an edge device with optimized deep learning models (SSD for object detection and MediaPipe for hand gesture recognition) to obtain flight control commands like takeoff, landing, hover, and tracking commands directly without the need of any controller or ground station. Based on flight tests and including initial evaluations, the system performs satisfactorily, considering low-latency control loops for different operating conditions, high recognition accuracy over a range of lighting environments, and reliable tracking during flight. This experimental study demonstrates the deploy ability of edge AI to enable continuous and completely self-sustaining human-machine interaction.

title: Smart UAV Surveillance Platform with Onboard Object Detection and Geofencing for Public Safety
authors: P Pal Pandian; Sam Philip
venue: International Conference on Computational Innovations and Sustainable Technologies (ICCIST)
abstract: Modern public safety operations are also changing due to the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) into the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) enabling maneuverability, open area, and continuous surveillance. The apparently exact plan and assessment of a clever UAV watchdog platform with on-board article locating, autonomous navigation using geofences, and edge processing will be introduced in this paper. The proposed system will be composed of a Pixhawk flight controller, a u-blox M10 GNSS module to provide navigation capabilities, and NVIDIA Jetson to run high-definition aerial video processing, specifically to recognize and use a YOLO-based detection pipeline. A simulated environment of a public event was used to test the accuracy of detection, inference latency, detection of anomalies and geofencing compliance across different environmental and crowd circumstances. The results of experiments also show average detection accuracy rates of 93.42%, inference delays of less than 60 ms, and few boundary violations, confirming the use of the system in responsive and secure use of aerial monitoring. The open-source modular nature of the platform permits the addition of other sensors and its subsequent expansion ability into multi-drone collaborative applications to note the prospects of such low-cost systems to influence large scale event tracking, disaster relief and urban security applications.

title: Autonomous Target Detection in Drone-Based Warfare Systems Using OpenCV and Deep Learning Object Detection Frameworks
authors: Vipul Barmukh; Shagufta Mohammad Sayeed Sheikh; Aum Patil; Prithviraj Chavan
venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
abstract: Abstract Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones, have fundamentally transformed the landscape of modern warfare through the integration of real-time computer vision and artificial intelligence. This paper presents a critical analysis and technical framework for autonomous target detection in drone-based warfare systems, leveraging OpenCV, YOLO (You Only Look Once), and deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). We investigate the implementation of real-time object detection pipelines aboard edge-deployed platforms such as NVIDIA Jetson, examining performance trade-offs between detection accuracy (mAP) and inference latency under battlefield constraints including low-altitude imaging, thermal signatures, and occlusion. Our system achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 87.3% on the VisDrone2023 benchmark dataset at 28.6 FPS on embedded hardware. We additionally propose a lightweight Temporal Consistency Filter (TCF) that suppresses spurious detections across consecutive frames, yielding a further 2.1% mAP improvement with negligible latency overhead. Comprehensive ablation studies are conducted to isolate the contribution of each pipeline component—preprocessing, backbone depth, quantization strategy, and post-processing—providing practitioners with actionable design guidance. We critically evaluate ethical concerns, failure modes, adversarial vulnerabilities, and International Humanitarian Law (IHL) compliance challenges associated with autonomous lethal systems, offering a balanced assessment of the current state of the art and future research directions. Index Terms UAV, drone warfare, OpenCV, YOLO, object detection, autonomous systems, computer vision, edge AI, VisDrone, convolutional neural networks, IHL compliance, temporal consistency filtering, model quantization, adversarial robustness.

title: Dual-LSTM Enhanced Adaptive Continuous Higher-Order Sliding Mode for Integrated Guidance and Control of Autonomous Aerospace Vehicles
authors: Mohamad Mahdi Soori; Seyed Hossein Sadati
venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
abstract: This article presents a robust Adaptive Continuous Higher-Order Sliding Mode Control (ACHOSMC) framework augmented with a Dual Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture for the integrated guidance and control (IGC) of autonomous aerospace vehicles. Unlike traditional static-gain methods, the proposed system employs two independently trained LSTM networks to dynamically schedule the boundary-layer and switching gains in real-time. This dual-channel adaptation enables the controller to proactively compensate for severe aerodynamic nonlinearities and stochastic disturbances while effectively suppressing chattering. Theoretical stability is rigorously established via an Input-to-State Stability (ISS)–Lyapunov analysis, ensuring uniform ultimate boundedness (UUB) of tracking errors. Extensive high-fidelity six-degree-of freedom (6-DOF) Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that the ACHOSMC–LSTM outperforms state-of-the-art neural baselines, achieving a 53.5% reduction in Integrated Time Absolute Error (ITAE) and an 18.2% decrease in terminal miss distance. Furthermore, embedded hardware implementation on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano confirms operational feasibility with an average inference latency of 3.82 ms, validating the system's suitability for real-time onboard deployment.

title: HTESGS–6DICVP: Offline Predictive Edge Safety Framework for Smartphone NPUs
authors: Anupam Sarma
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Recent advances in mobile hardware enable smartphones to perform real-time artificial intelligence inference using on-device neural accelerators. This paper presents the HTESGS–6DICVP architecture, an offline predictive edge safety framework designed for smartphones equipped with Neural Processing Units (NPUs). The framework integrates lightweight computer vision, contextual state modeling, probabilistic Bayesian risk estimation, and deterministic safety logic to detect and predict hazardous situations in real time. Analytical modeling demonstrates that the architecture can operate with approximately 62 ms inference latency and under 250 MB memory footprint, making it suitable for deployment on mid-range smartphones. title: Enhancing Rail Transit Safety: Edge Computing‐Based Driver State Monitoring System
authors: Yiqing Liu; Gaoyun Cheng; Binbin Yuan; Hongyu Sun; E J C Stewart; Zhe Fu; Zongru Ma; Ning Bo Zhao
abstract: ABSTRACT Ensuring the safety and alertness of railway drivers is essential, yet many existing monitoring systems still experience noticeable delays, limited real‐time performance, and inefficient use of communication resources. To address these challenges, we present a rail transit driver state monitoring system that integrates edge computing with cloud‐based management. The system employs multiple onboard cameras, including a cabin surveillance camera and an AI assisted camera that tracks the driver's movements, to provide a broad view of driver and cabin activity. A Jetson Orin edge unit performs real‐time inference using deep learning models for driver authentication, facial‐state analysis, behaviour recognition, and cabin personnel monitoring. To reduce bandwidth consumption, the system transmits compact feature representations during normal operation and uploads raw video to the cloud only when abnormal events are detected, enabling network‐wide supervision via a central platform. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed edge‐first pipeline achieves an average end‐to‐end decision latency of 173.73 ms on the edge device, while maintaining strong detection performance on the test set, reaching 96.82% accuracy for blink detection, 98.33% accuracy for yawn detection, and 97.22% accuracy for driver behaviour monitoring.

title: An Embedded AI Perception Framework for Autonomous Long-Range Loitering Munition Strike Systems Operating in Cluttered and GNSS-Denied Environments
authors: A. S. Imam; O. A. Ogunleye; A. Surajo; I. A. Ibrahim; Muhammad Ahmad Baballe
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Autonomous long-range loitering munition systems require robust onboard perception architectures capable of detecting, classifying, and discriminating tactical targets under cluttered battlefield environments while operating within strict computational and power constraints. This paper presents the design and implementation framework of an embedded artificial-intelligence-enabled vision pipeline for real-time onboard target detection in enduranceclass autonomous strike UAV platforms. The proposed architecture integrates lightweight deep learning objectdetection networks, multi-sensor preprocessing, confidence-driven discrimination logic, and GPU-accelerated edge-inference modules to enable reliable perception in GNSS-degraded and communication-limited operational environments. Simulation-based evaluation demonstrates that optimised convolutional neural-network detectors achieve inference latency below 120 ms with detection precision exceeding 90% under cluttered terrain conditions. The framework establishes a scalable baseline for indigenous development of autonomous loitering munition strike perception systems supporting ISR-strike convergence architectures.

title: Spatiotemporal Attention‐Based CNN‐BiLSTM Model for Robust Lane and Obstacle Detection in IoV‐Enabled Autonomous Driving
authors: Suresh kulandaivelu; Syied Mazar; N. Sangeetha; Sathiyapriya Rajavelu; Anita Garhwal
abstract: For safe operation in resource-constrained and changing environments, self-driving cars in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks require accurate and effective perception systems. However, under poor environmental conditions such as” different light, interference by weather, and occlusion of scenes, traditional vision-based models often fall short performing below par. Here, spatiotemporal attention-enhanced convolutional neural network (CNN)–bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) is introduced that combines attention-based refinement, bidirectional temporal context modeling, and spatial feature extraction. For improved motion understanding, the BiLSTM extracts forward and backward temporal relations, and the CNN module pools dense visual features of adjacent frames. These are followed by a multihead spatial attention mechanism that identifies salient regions, i.e., traffic lanes and moving objects. A series of tests were performed using an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier edge computer on the BDD100K and KITTI datasets in a simulated IoV environment. Following optimization, the suggested model achieved a model size of 48 MB, real-time inference speed of 26 frames per second, lane detection intersection over union of 84.7%, F1 score of 91.3%, object detection mean average precision (mAP)@0.5 of 78.6%, and mAP@0.75 of 69.2%. These findings indicate that the model is superior to current baselines in terms of accuracy, computational efficiency, and temporal robustness and thus could be used in real-world autonomous IoV applications.

title: Lightweight Dual-YOLOv8 Instance-Aware Semantic Segmentation for Real-Time Autonomous Driving on Edge ARM/GPU Platforms
authors: Safa Teboulbi; Seifeddine Messaoud; Mohamed Ali Hajjaji; Mohamed Atri; Abdellatif Mtibaa
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a fundamental component of autonomous driving systems, enabling accurate scene understanding and object-level perception. However, achieving precise instance-level delineation while maintaining real-time performance on resource-constrained platforms remains a significant challenge, particularly for edge deployment scenarios. This paper proposes a lightweight dual-YOLOv8 fusion framework for instance-aware semantic segmentation in autonomous driving applications. The proposed approach integrates YOLOv8n-seg and YOLOv8s-seg through a multi-scale fusion strategy that exploits their complementary feature representations to improve the segmentation of road-relevant objects, including cars, buses, trucks, and motorcycles. The framework is evaluated on the Reetiquetado de Vehiculos dataset using standard instance-level segmentation metrics. Experimental results demonstrate strong performance, achieving an overall mAP@0.5 of 92.9% and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 80.8%, while maintaining real-time inference with an average processing time of 7.9 ms per image (126 FPS) on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 GPU. Class-wise and confidence-based analyses confirm consistent segmentation accuracy across vehicle categories, highlighting the robustness of the proposed fusion strategy in handling scale variation, occlusions, and object diversity. In addition, an embedded deployment analysis provides insight into the feasibility and practical constraints of deploying the proposed framework on representative edge platforms. Overall, the proposed dual-YOLOv8 fusion framework achieves an effective balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time autonomous driving perception on edge ARM/GPU platforms and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS).

title: YOLO on GPU Implementation for a Vision-Based Fruit Select and Place System with a 5-DOF Robotic Arm
authors: Shubham Panigrahi; Akash Biyani; Ashutosh Mithari; Sonali Sawant; Sunil L. Tade; Mahesh T. Kolte
venue: International Conference on Computing Communication Control and automation
abstract: This article introduces a cost-effective approach for a vision-guided robotic pick-and-place arm and demonstrates how this produces a faster inference rate and greater efficiency than existing products, which are typically constructed with rather high-end equipment. A YOLOv4-tiny algorithm-based object detection model is trained to classify and localise the desired object using a custom-created dataset. A monocular camera was also calibrated to determine its intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, which facilitated the determination of coordinates. GPU-based NVIDIA Jetson NANO is utilised to process the live stream captured by a camera, not only due to its faster inference capability and computations but also because of its quicker inference capability. The fabrication of 5-degree-of-freedom robotic limb results in improved positioning, more precise target object placement, and a larger work envelope. This arrangement identifies and localises the target object within the image frame by recognising it in its surroundings. Later, the image coordinates are mapped to real-world coordinates and fed to the robotic arm, which applies the appropriate inverse kinematics to plan the trajectory and implement the pick-and-place task. This low-cost system resulted in 40 frames per second of real-time inference speed, which is nearly double that of existing models.

title: A multimodal non-contact safety monitoring system for industrial personnel status detection
authors: Chun Hu; Jiali Wang; Kang Ma; Dezhi Zheng; Peng Peng
abstract: To address the intelligent and real-time monitoring demands of personnel status in complex industrial environments, this paper proposes a novel multimodal safety monitoring system that innovatively integrates head pose recognition and mmwave radar based vital sign detection within an edge-deployable framework. The system introduces a rule-driven fusion strategy at the decision level, enabling interpretable and efficient state inference from heterogeneous modalities. The proposed approach supports synchronous processing of visual and radar data on the Jetson AGX Orin edge computing platform, ensuring low-latency and high-reliability operation in dynamic industrial scenarios. Additionally, a 3D-printed mechanical enclosure is designed for robust deployment in real-world environments. Experimental results demonstrate an average behaviour classification accuracy of 91.3% and a stable runtime frame rate of 25 FPS, validating the system’s practical applicability, scalability, and real-time performance.

title: Vision Beyond Darkness: Low-Light Object Detection for Heavy-Duty Vehicle Safety
authors: A B David Josva; R Karthik; R. Vidhya; Naveena Nagulan; S. Sam Peter; T. Raghunathan
venue: International Conference on Emerging Research in Computational Science (ICERCS)
abstract: The high-duty vehicles are often used under adverse conditions like tunnels, highways and industrial areas where the low luminance and visual noise are major causes of poor object detection. Regular eyesight and sensors cannot achieve reliability in such circumstances and make collisions and circumstances of operation a greater risk. In this paper, an AI-driven low-light object detection system will be proposed to improve the visibility and safety of heavy-duty vehicles. The given system combines a deep convolutional neural network (Zero-DCE++) to improve adaptive illumination with a real-time object detector model (YOLOv11) trained on the datasets in low-light scenarios including exDark, FLIR Thermal and BDD100K. Experiments have shown that the optimized detection pipeline attains a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 0.78 and is significantly more accurate than traditional models yet retains almost real-time inference in an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX system. The findings demonstrate that AI-based low-light vision systems have a high potential to make night-time and tunnel driving much safer on heavy duty vehicles due to better perception, quick response, and consistent obstacle detection.

title: Edge AI-Based Real-Time Speed Estimation and License Plate Recognition for Urban Road Safety in ASEAN Cities
authors: Aran Asavanarakul; Prach Asavanarakul; Phongsuk Ampha
abstract: Road accidents in low-speed community zones account for over 60% of incidents in Southeast Asian cities, yet they remain underexplored in intelligent transportation research. This paper presents a cross-regional Edge AI framework for real-time vehicle speed estimation and license plate recognition (LPR) to improve urban road safety. The system integrates YOLOv8-based visual inference with frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar on an embedded Jetson Xavier NX platform. A geometry-driven normalization pipeline, combined with character-region masking and coordinate-based sequencing, enhances generalization across different plate formats and lighting conditions without retraining. Experimental results show accuracy degradation below 10% between domestic and foreign datasets, outperforming prior works that typically reported 10-15% degradation under domain shift. The model achieves 94.9% accuracy, PSIS > 0.95, and inference latency of 58 ms (end-to-end$\approx 74 ~\text{ms}$) with power consumption under 20 W, confirming real-time feasibility for edge deployment. These findings validate that geometry-aware normalization provides a transferable and efficient approach for AI-based traffic perception, supporting ASEAN Smart Mobility initiatives and enabling scalable deployment from Bangkok to other regional metropolitan areas.

title: RT-OCR : Real-Time OCR Pipeline with Formal Timing Guarantees for Edge Vision Systems
authors: Eya Ben Hmida; Sarra Abidi; Leila Jemni Ben Ayed
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Deep learning OCR achieves high accuracy but exhibits unpredictable latency, preventing deployment in safety-critical systems like autonomous vehicles and industrial robotics. RT-OCR provides formal worst-case execution time (WCET) bounds on edge platforms through a timing-aware pipeline architecture, adaptive workload controller, and measurement-based WCET characterization on Jetson Nano and Raspberry Pi 5. Evalua- tion demonstrates 73% jitter reduction, 32% WCET improvement, and 97.5% accuracy with 100% deadline compliance across 10,000 consecutive frames.

title: OccMALA: An Efficient 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction Method with Linear Complexity for Perception on Autonomous Ground Platforms
authors: Guosheng Liu; Yunzhe Xiong; Jiefei Ma
venue: International Conference on Computer, Artificial Intelligence and Control Engineering (CAICE)
abstract: For autonomous ground platforms operating in scenarios such as unmanned inspection and delivery, efficient and accurate perception of the surrounding environment's geometric structure and semantic information is essential. Compared to general 3D object detection methods, 3D semantic occupancy prediction excels at modeling irregular objects and providing precise semantic information, thus emerging as a mainstream approach in autonomous driving perception. However, most existing 3D semantic occupancy prediction methods are constructed based on 3D CNNs or Transformers, which impose high computational and memory demands. This makes them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained small autonomous ground platforms and limits their global modeling capabilities. To address the issues of high computational complexity and poor global modeling in current methods, we propose a lightweight and efficient occupancy prediction network named OccMALA. The contributions are threefold: First, we explicitly decouple the learning processes of semantic segmentation and scene completion, and train them with multi-scale supervision separately. Second, to tackle the high computational cost and memory consumption associated with voxel feature extraction, we project voxel features into the Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) space to reduce computational overhead. Third, for efficient feature extraction and fusion of semantic segmentation and scene completion features, we introduce the BEV-MALA module to enhance BEV features and propose the U-MALA architecture for adaptive multi-scale BEV feature fusion. Extensive experiments on the SemanticKITTI benchmark demonstrate that OccMALA achieves a 0.4% improvement in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) compared to the current mainstream LiDAR-based method, SSC-RS. More importantly, it significantly boosts the inference speed by 40.1%. Furthermore, we deploy OccMALA on an autonomous ground platform equipped with the NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX as its onboard computer, where it achieves a real-time inference time of 53.8 ms, representing a 35.3% improvement over SSC-RS, while maintaining a lower GPU memory consumption.

title: A Path Planning Approach for Context Aware Autonomous UAVs used for Surveying Areas in Developing Regions
authors: Fredrika Kringberg
venue: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
abstract: Developing regions are often characterized by large areas that are poorly reachable or explored. The mapping and census of roaming populations in these areas are often difficult and sporadic. A recent spark in the development of small aerial vehicles has made them the perfect tool to efficiently and accurately monitor these areas. This paper presents an approach to aid area surveying through the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles. The two main components of this approach are an efficient on-device deep learning object identification component to capture and infer images with acceptable performance (latency andaccuracy), and a dynamic path planning approach, informed by the object identification component. In particular, this thesis illustrates the development of the path planning component, which exploits potential field methods to dynamically adapt the path based on inputs from the vision system. It also describes the integration work that was performed to implement the approach on a prototype platform, with the aim to achieve autonomous flight with onboard computation. The path planning component was developed with the purpose of gaining information about the populations detected by the object identification component, while considering the limited resources of energy and computational power onboard a UAV. The developed algorithm was compared to navigation using a predefined path, where the UAV does not react to the environment. Results from the comparison show that the algorithm provide more information about the objects of interest, with a very small change in flight time. The integration of the object identification and the path planning components on the prototype platform was evaluated in terms of end-to-end latency, power consumption and resource utilization. Results show that the proposed approach is feasible for area surveying in developing regions. Parts of this work has been published in the workshop of DroNet, collocated with MobiSys, with the title Surveying Areas in Developing Regions Through Context Aware Drone Mobility. Thework was carried out in collaboration with Alessandro Montanari, Alice Valentini, Cecilia Mascoloand Amanda Prorok.
