title: Generative AI-Native Edge Sensors: Collaborative Data Reconstruction via Lightweight Federated Learning
authors: Jiaming Pei; Minxi Feng; M. Pounambal; Venkata Krishna Parimala; Minghui Dai
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Areas in Sensors
abstract: The reliability of time-series data streams in distributed Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks is frequently compromised by sensor faults and unstable communication, leading to critical data gaps. Traditional centralized approaches for data reconstruction introduce high latency and data privacy risks, failing to meet the requirements of resource-constrained edge environments. To address this, we propose a novel Lightweight Federated Generative Learning (LFGL) framework, termed FedGen Sensor, which enables collaborative, privacy-preserving, andresilient data reconstruction directly on heterogeneous edge sensor nodes. Our framework employs a lightweight Variational Autoencoder (VAE) optimized for temporal data and integrates a deep Hardware-Software Co-Design approach. Specifically, we utilize an aggressive compression strategy combining INT8 Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) and sparse update transmission to drastically reduce the model's footprint. Validated on a physical testbed comprising ESP32 microcontrollers and Raspberry Pi servers, FedGen-Sensor demonstrates superior performance: it achieves data reconstruction fidelity (RMSE) comparable to the standard FP32 FedAvg baseline (0.086 vs. 0.082), while simultaneously reducing communication overhead by 5.5×, and cutting the average edge inference latency by 2.5×. This work validates the feasibility of embedding sophisticated generative intelligence directly onto ultra low-power edge sensors, setting a new paradigm for autonomous and resilient IoT data services.

title: Edge AI Wildlife Classification with FPGA-Based Deterministic Deterrence on PYNQ-Z2
authors: Palle Devi Sri Vinay Mohan Reddy; Bonthu Namo Sai Reddy; Chakilela Sairaj; Ngangbam Phalguni Singh; Vijay Rao Kumbhare
venue: International Symposium on VLSI Design and Test (VDAT)
abstract: Human-wildlife conflict in a g ricultural re gions results in significant c r op d a mage, p a rticularly i n re mote areas lacking stable infrastructure. This work presents an edge AIbased wildlife classification a ndde terrence prototype designed for low-power, offline d eployment. A M obileNetV2 convolutional neural network (CNN) is trained to classify nine wildlife species associated with farm intrusion and optimized using full-integer INT8 quantization for efficient e m bedded i n ference. T h eoptimized model is deployed on the PYNQ-Z2 platform based on the Xilinx Zynq-7000 SoC, performing on-device inference using TensorFlow Lite on the ARM Cortex-A9 processor without cloud dependency. Experimental validation demonstrates high classification a c curacy wi th a compact model si ze of 2.74 MB achieving an average inference latency of approximately 680 ms per frame and an estimated power consumption of approximately 2.5 W. A species-specific d eterrence c ontrol l ayer is implemented in the Programmable Logic (PL) using a custom Register Transfer Level (RTL) based finite s tate m achine, i ntegrated with the Processing System (PS) via the AXI-Lite interface, enabling deterministic low-latency GPIO actuation independent of Linux software scheduling delays. The post-implementation analysis demonstrates that the hardware controller occupies only 1.09% LUT utilization on the Zynq-7020 programmable logic fabric. The results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying lightweight wildlife classification s ystems on r esource-constrained embedded platforms for autonomous agricultural monitoring applications.

title: Smart Automated Garden Entity
authors: NAGALINGAM HARSHADITH; THALLURI RAHUL; THOTAKURI PRAVEEN KUMAR; T. VASAVI; B. Pooja
venue: JOURNAL OF ADVANCE AND FUTURE RESEARCH
abstract: Reducing the latency between disease detection and remedial action is critical for preventing crop loss in precision agriculture. This paper introduces the Smart Automated Garden Entity, an AIoT system developed for real-time monitoring and autonomous management of plant health. While traditional classifiers often rely on static image processing, Smart Automated Garden Entity utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) optimized for edge deployment, enabling live video inference across 38 distinct plant pathologies. The system employs a multi-threaded architecture to synchronize visual detection with environmental data—including soil moisture, temperature, and humidity—collected at 500 millisecond intervals via an Arduino-based sensor node. By cross-referencing visual symptoms with environmental context, the system improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces false positives common in variable lighting. When stress vectors are identified, Smart Automated Garden Entity executes autonomous interventions, such as triggering irrigation relays, while simultaneously using the Gemini API to provide localized remedial advice to a user dashboard. Experimental results demonstrate a response time of under 1.5 seconds from detection to intervention, suggesting that the system is a viable low-latency solution for automated small-scale agriculture.

title: Edge-Enhanced Federated Optimization for Real-Time Silver-Haired Whirlwind Trip
authors: Xiaolong Chen; Hongfeng Zhang; Cora Un In Wong; Hongbo Ge
abstract: We propose an edge-enhanced federated learning framework for real-time itinerary optimization in elderly oriented adventure tourism, addressing the critical need for adaptive scheduling that balances activity intensity with health constraints. The system integrates lightweight convolutional neural networks with a priority-based scheduling algorithm, processing participant profiles and real-time biometric data through a decentralized computation model to enable dynamic adjustments. A modified Hungarian algorithm incorporates physical exertion scores, temporal proximity weights, and health risk factors, then optimizes activity assignments while respecting physiological recovery requirements. The federated learning architecture operates across distributed edge nodes, preserving data privacy through localized model training and periodic global aggregation. Furthermore, the framework interfaces with transportation systems and medical monitoring infrastructure, automatically triggering itinerary modifications when vital sign anomalies exceed adaptive thresholds. Implemented on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin modules, the system achieves 300 ms end-to-end latency for real-time schedule updates, meeting stringent safety requirements for elderly participants. The proposed method demonstrates significant improvements over conventional itinerary planners through its edge computing efficiency and personalized adaptation capabilities, particularly in handling the latency-sensitive demands of intensive tourism scenarios. Experimental results show robust performance across diverse participant profiles and activity types, confirming the system’s practical viability for real-world deployment in elderly adventure tourism operations.

title: PSTA-VS: Position-Aware Spatiotemporal Attention for Efficient Video Summarization in Internet of Vehicles
authors: Wenhao Shao; Xiaoyu Zhou; Pengyu Yang; Yongguo Ling; Mengzhu Wang; Jiawei Su; Yutao Zhang; Xiulai Wang
abstract: Internet of Vehicles (IoV) systems generate massive volumes of video streams, posing significant challenges to real-time decision-making and data management in resource-constrained autonomous driving scenarios. Existing video summarization methods often struggle to capture long-term dependencies due to inherent information redundancy and complex dynamic variations across frames. To address these issues, we propose a novel framework termed Position-Aware Spatio-Temporal Attention for Video Summarization (PSTA-VS). PSTA-VS enhances feature representations by progressively integrating multi-dimensional attention mechanisms to capture long-term dependencies effectively. Specifically, the framework introduces two core components: 1) Global Dependency Encoding (GDE), which models cross-dimensional spatiotemporal correlations across the entire sequence to preserve comprehensive contextual information; and 2) Position-Aware Attention (PAA), which adaptively assigns weights to critical frames and spatial regions while suppressing redundant content. By seamlessly fusing these mechanisms, PSTA-VS generates coherent, information-rich summaries. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that PSTA-VS outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Inference latency and edge-deployment evaluations on two additional datasets further confirm its responsiveness and lightweight design. By avoiding complex stacked architectures, PSTA-VS offers an efficient and scalable solution for visual understanding in resource-limited IoV environments.

title: A Security-Centric Perspective on AI and Blockchain Integration with Network Infrastructure Security in 5G and IoT Edge Environments
authors: Omkar Singh; Col. Rahul Sharma
venue: Journal of Advances in Computer Networks
abstract: With blockchain technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) coming together, the digital world is changing quickly and opening up new possibilities for secure, autonomous, and decentralized systems. This paper examines the integration of these disruptive technologies from a security perspective, examining how they might enhance data integrity, privacy, and trust, particularly in light of new network infrastructures like 5G and Internet of Things (IoT) edge settings. The study examines the security flaws in blockchain and Artificial Intelligence (AI) alone and together, highlighting how combining the two can both increase and decrease risks. The difficulties of protecting information and computation across dispersed, low-latency edge nodes in 5G-enabled IoT systems are specifically discussed. The report outlines the main dangers, real-world applications, and future research avenues needed to create reliable and scalable AI-blockchain frameworks for contemporary communication networks. It concludes that strong approaches to interoperability, secure edge deployment, governance, and infrastructure resilience are necessary to fully realise the potential of these technologies.

title: OPTIMIZING NVIDIA® GEFORCE RTX™ 5090 & "AMD RX 9070"for machine learning and artificial intelligence workload
authors: Mohit Jain; Adit Shah; Brahaspati Dev; Ram Kumar; Mathew Campisi
venue: World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences
abstract: As consumer-grade GPUs have rapidly evolved, efforts have emerged to deploy these computational models for training and inference, typically handled by data center hardware. The paper explores optimization of two next-generation graphics computing units, the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 and the AMD Radeon RX 9070, to optimize the new generation of ML and AI applications. We examine the internal compute pipelines, tensor/matrix acceleration capabilities, memory hierarchies, and software ecosystems (CUDA/cuDNN/TensorRT versus ROCm/MIOpen/HIP) that influence ML performance in a two-pronged architectural and empirical study. The convolutional networks, transformer models, diffusion architecture, and graph neural networks share a standard benchmarking model: training, inference latency, power consumption, precision scaling (FP32-INT8), and bottlenecks. The results of the experiment have demonstrated that the performance profiles of the RTX 5090 and the RX 9070 are different, i.e., the acceleration performance of mixed precision and kernel fusion is higher in the RTX 5090 as compared to the throughput performance of the RX 9070 in the BF16/INT8 workloads with the high memory-bandwidth utilization. Strategies for each platform. Platform-specific optimization strategies, such as kernel tuning, compiler optimization, memory prefetching, gradient checkpointing, and scaling to multiple GPUs, are developed and evaluated. Further, two case studies of real-world performance tuning of transformer fine-tuning and diffusion model inference are also presented. The findings highlight that hardware alone does not guarantee the best ML performance; effective optimization can deliver performance gains that are even more significant than raw compute alone. The paper will provide a step-by-step roadmap for practitioners, researchers, and engineers who may want to optimize the application of RTX 5090 and RX 9070 in artificial intelligence algorithms, as well as a future perspective on the standard models of unified programming on GPUs and emergent precision formats.

title: Radarnext: lightweight and real-time 3D object detector based on 4D mmWave imaging radar
authors: Liye Jia; Runwei Guan; Haocheng Zhao; Qiuchi Zhao; Ka Lok Man; Jeremy Smith; Yu Liu; Yutao Yue
venue: EURASIP Journal on Advances in Signal Processing
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) object detection is essential for autonomous driving (AD) and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). However, most existing 3D object detection works primarily focus more on the detection accuracy than on the detection efficiency, although the latter is also a critical metric for practical applications. In this paper, we propose RadarNeXt, a lightweight and real-time 3D object detector based on 4D millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar point clouds. We introduce a re-parameterization mechanism in the feature extraction process to enhance inference efficiency while maintaining the multi-branch architecture’s capability to construct multi-scale features. Moreover, to emphasize the irregular foreground features of radar point clouds, and to suppress background clutter, we present a Multi-path Deformable Foreground Enhancement Network (MDFEN), ensuring high detection accuracy while minimizing the trade-off in speed and limiting the number of extensional parameters. Experimental results show that RadarNeXt can achieve the outstanding efficiency performance of over 67 frames per second (FPS) on a RTX A4000 GPU and over 28 FPS on the Jetson AGX Orin. Notably, RadarNeXt meets the real-time inference requirements while achieving more than 50 mean average precision (mAP) on the View-of-Delft (VoD) dataset and over 32 mAP on the TJ4DRadSet (TJ4D) dataset. This research demonstrates that RadarNeXt represents a novel and effective paradigm for 3D object detection based on 4D mmWave radar.

title: Embodied AI Launcher: A Tool for Modeling, Simulation, and Deployment Evaluation of Transformer-Based Embodied AI Tasks at the Edge: Tool Paper
authors: Byeonggil Jun; Deeksha Prahlad; Mehdi Ghasemi; Hokeun Kim
venue: Forum on specification and Design Languages
abstract: Embodied AI agents in robotic cyber-physical systems (CPSs) increasingly rely on transformer-based models such as large language models (LLMs) and vision transformers (ViTs). Their high computational demands, real-time constraints, task dependencies, and communication costs make task orchestration across heterogeneous platforms challenging. This paper presents Embodied AI Launcher, an open-source tool for modeling, simulating, and deployment evaluation of transformer-based embodied-agent workloads. The tool supports DAG-structured task models with device-dependent execution times, deadlines, input/output data sizes, and communication costs, and evaluates centralized scheduling strategies across heterogeneous computing nodes. For each configuration, Embodied AI Launcher visualizes per-device computation and communication timelines and reports deadline outcomes, enabling direct comparison across schedulers. We demonstrate the tool on transformer-based embodied AI workloads distributed across heterogeneous platforms, including a Jetson AGX Orin and GPU-equipped edge servers, and show both scalable simulation and dataflow deployment tracing. Embodied AI Launcher is publicly available as open-source software.

title: Beyond Obstacle Alerts: Multi-Modal Visual Question Answering for Assistive Navigation
authors: Samyuktha Jagannath; G Anitha
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Computational Networks (ICISCN)
abstract: Visually impaired people face huge barriers to autonomy in navigation, in part because of a limited awareness of the various dynamic obstructions, space topology, and the surrounding scene. The traditional assistive devices are also imperative alerts or sensor-based detection methods, which can be normally followed by cognitive overload, disjointed scene understanding and poor handling of time hazards. This research presents NAVQA, a multimodal Visual Question Answering framework specifically designed for assistive navigation. The system integrates real-time object detection using YOLOv8n and monocular depth estimation using MiDaS, together with ResNet-18-based localization against a pre-built knowledge base and graph-based path planning. At its core, NAVQA introduces a risk-modulated cross-modal transformer that dynamically scales attention weights using Time-to-Collision (TTC) priors and a reinforcement-learned adaptive query selector that jointly optimises semantic relevance, safety gain, and cognitive-load reduction. Unlike prior AVQA pipelines that rely on standard attention or generic reinforcement learning, our framework delivers explicit safety-aware fusion and edge-optimised query prioritisation. Deployed on NVIDIA Jetson Nano, it achieves$\mathbf{9 0. 3 \%}$collision avoidance,$\mathbf{8 7. 2 \%}$query relevance, 2.8% redundancy, and sub- 500 ms end-to-end latency. Ablation studies confirm that the risk-modulated attention and adaptive selection modules each contribute more than 8 % performance gains over baselines, establishing NAVQA as the first end-to-end, safetyprioritised multimodal VQA system for assistive navigation.

title: Real-Time Drone Communication System Using ROS 2 and GStreamer with YOLOv8-Seg for Face Segmentation
authors: Husam Salah Mahdi; Kontham Raja Kumar; K. John David Christopher
venue: International Journal of Computational and Experimental Science and Engineering
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a ROS 2-based UAV syste m for real-time video streaming and intelligentground station processing. The proposed architecture integrates a Raspberry Pi 3 onboard computer with a Jetson Orin Nanoground station over a wireless network. Video is captured and encoded using GStreamer on the UAV, streamed over UDP, anddecoded on the ground station for real-time object detection using the YOLOv8-seg model. ROS 2 middleware facilitatessynchronized telemetry and camera communication between the UAV and ground station via DDS topics. The systemdemonstrates low-latency video transmission (∼105 ms), high streaming frame rate (30 FPS), and real-time object detection at28–30 FPS with an average precision of 81.2%. The modularity of ROS 2 enables easy integration of additional perception,control, and autonomous decision-making modules. Experimental results validate the system’s performance for surveillance andinspection tasks, showcasing the potential of open-source middleware and embedded AI for edge-enhanced UAV applications.

title: EdgeCurator: Efficient Cross-Modal Grounding for Real-Time Language-Guided UAV Navigation
authors: Sitian Peng; Rui Wang
abstract: Deploying cross-modal representations on a micro Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) requires accurate language–vision alignment and low-latency inference under tight compute constraints. Heavy Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide strong semantic reasoning but are often unsuitable for an onboard control loop, whereas lightweight visual backbones commonly defer language fusion to a separate planning stage. We present EdgeCurator, a compact end-to-end early-fusion framework for real-time language-guided UAV navigation in access-controlled indoor spaces. Its Semantic-Spatial Grounding (SSG) Head converts lightweight text embeddings into semantic queries and uses conditioned deformable cross-attention to sparsely sample multi-scale visual features. On the custom Expo-VLN benchmark, EdgeCurator uses 14.8M parameters, runs at 54 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, and reaches 67.3% grounding accuracy and 62.8% navigation success. We additionally report 60 controlled physical trials with two target types, achieving 78.3% success. These trials test onboard Sim2Real feasibility for pre-opening inspection and curation assistance; they do not establish operation around visitors or generalization to full exhibition deployments. The results position EdgeCurator as an efficiency-oriented cross-modal representation and grounding system for resource-constrained aerial agents.

title: MAPLE-Edge: A Runtime Latency Predictor for Edge Devices
authors: Saeejith Nair; Saad Abbasi; Alexander M. Wong; Mohammad Javad Shafiee
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has enabled automatic discovery of more efficient neural network architectures, especially for mobile and embedded vision applications. Although recent research has proposed ways of quickly estimating latency on unseen hardware devices with just a few samples, little focus has been given to the challenges of estimating latency on runtimes using optimized graphs, such as TensorRT and specifically for edge devices. As devices like NVIDIA’s Jetsons get more popular in embedded computing and robotics, we observe a pressing need to more accurately estimate inference latency of neural network architectures on diverse runtimes, including highly optimized ones. In this work, we propose MAPLE-Edge, an edge device-oriented extension of MAPLE, the state-of-the-art latency predictor for general purpose hardware, where we train a regression network on architecture-latency pairs in conjunction with a hardware-runtime descriptor to effectively estimate latency on a diverse pool of edge devices. Compared to MAPLE, MAPLE-Edge can describe the runtime and target device platform using a much smaller set of CPU performance counters that are widely available on all Linux kernels, while still achieving up to +49.6% accuracy gains against previous state-of-the-art baseline methods on optimized edge device runtimes, using just 10 measurements from an unseen target device. We also demonstrate that unlike MAPLE which performs best when trained on a pool of devices sharing a common runtime, MAPLE-Edge can effectively generalize across runtimes by applying a trick of normalizing performance counters by the operator latency, in the measured hardware-runtime descriptor. Lastly, we show that for runtimes exhibiting lower than desired accuracy, performance can be boosted by collecting additional samples from the target device, with an extra 90 samples translating to gains of nearly +40%.

title: Retracted: AI-Native 6G Networks: Adaptive Resource Allocation Through Edge-Integrated Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Anurag Shrivastava; Zaid Ajzan Alsalami; Rallabandi Venkata Santoshi Saraswati Swetha Nagini; Aman Sharma; Irfan Khan; Mudra Gupta
venue: International Conference on Intelligent & Innovative Practices in Engineering & Management (IIPEM)
abstract: This paper investigates AI-Native 6G networks that integrate deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents at the network edge to achieve adaptive, low-latency, and energy-efficient resource allocation. We present a conceptual architecture—Edge-Integrated DRL (EIDRL)—that combines lightweight on-device policies, edge-hosted value models, and a hierarchical orchestration layer that mediates model updates, inference placement, and safety constraints. The proposed framework explicitly addresses 6G-era characteristics: massive heterogeneous devices, semantic and sensing-aided communications, integration of sensing/communication/computation (ISCC), and stringent reliability/latency requirements. We detail the learning formulation (state, action, reward, multi-timescale update rules), introduce techniques for sample-efficient training (model-based rollouts, transfer from foundation WLAMs, and federated/split learning hybrids), and propose mechanisms for safety, fairness, and compute-aware scheduling. Through analytical arguments and representative numerical scenarios (multi-tenant edge slices, ISAC nodes, and mobile user clusters), we demonstrate that EIDRL reduces regret relative to static baselines, lowers average latency under load, and improves spectral and energy efficiency when the edge controller coordinates inference placement and action aggregation. Finally, we identify open research directions—privacy-preserving multi-agent coordination, certifiable robustness of learned policies, semantics-aware reward design, and operational considerations for O-RAN/OAI integration—thereby providing a focused research agenda for adaptive resource allocation in AI-native 6G systems.

title: DANCE: A Lightweight Dynamic Adapter Network for Real-Time Traffic Accident Anticipation
authors: Hao-Yu Yen; Wen‐Hsien Fang; Yie‐Tarng Chen
abstract: Traffic accident anticipation is critical for proactive safety systems, yet remains challenging due to rapidly evolving scenes, transient accident precursors, and strict low-latency inference requirements. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Adapters for Neural CLIP Enhancement (DANCE), a lightweight end-to-end framework for real-time traffic accident anticipation. DANCE adopts a dual-branch architecture based on Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) and integrates a set of dynamic adapters to enable efficient task adaptation. To accommodate diverse driving scenarios, we introduce two input-aware mechanisms within the adapters: Dynamic Gating (DyG) and Dynamic Scaling (DyS). DyG acts as a content-conditioned soft routing mechanism that selectively emphasizes salient tokens while suppressing irrelevant noise, whereas DyS adaptively modulates the strength of residual contributions to balance pre-trained knowledge preservation and task-specific learning. Operating synergistically, these mechanisms enhance temporal sensitivity and semantic stability without compromising computational efficiency. In addition, lightweight adapters in the text encoder improve the alignment between risk-related textual queries and visual tokens, while a temporal refinement head stabilizes predictions over time. Two auxiliary objectives—a vision–text Contrastive Loss (CLoss) and a Gate Sparsity Loss (GSLoss)—are introduced to strengthen cross-modal consistency and improve feature selectivity. We also provide a discussion on framework properties, including the computational complexity, convergence, and stability of the proposed framework. Extensive experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that DANCE achieves competitive accuracy with improved early anticipation performance using only RGB inputs. Importantly, the proposed method achieves 41.19 effective FPS under a sliding-window streaming simulation on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, demonstrating a favorable trade-off between accuracy and efficiency among CLIP-based RGB–text approaches for real-time edge deployment.

title: A Portable LiDAR-Based Adverse Weather Perception System for Four-Wheelers with Multi-Stage Denoising
authors: Vivek Namburi; Ethish Rudraraju; Abhinav Pasumarthy; Kuldeep Devarasetty; N. Harini
venue: International Conference on Next Generation Electronics (NELEX)
abstract: This research presents a compact, real-time LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging)-based safety architecture that is simple to include into conventional four-wheeled vehicles. Situational awareness and vehicle safety are enhanced by the technology through trustworthy point-cloud visualization and trustworthy perception in bad weather. Unlike typical LiDAR implementations that deteriorate in heavy rain, fog, and dust, the proposed technique maintains dependability through adaptive filtering and efficient LiDAR processing. ROS2 is used on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano to create a three-stage pipeline for low-latency edge computation: voxel-grid downsampling, RANSAC ground segmentation, and statistical outlier removal. Experimental evaluation in a range of road settings shows an average processing delay of less than 100 ms, a detection accuracy of $91.7 \%$, and an $8.6 \%$ false-positive rate within a 30 m range. The results demonstrate a scalable, low-cost platform that may be applied to both personal and commercial vehicle applications.

title: An Intelligent Pantograph Condition Monitoring System for Locomotives Based on Domestic RK3588 Platform
authors: TIAN Ye; XU Zhensen; YUAN Xiaojun; LIU Leixinyuan; PAN Rongzhuang; LI Chen
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
abstract: Abnormal pantograph conditions in electric locomotives threaten train operational safety, yet existing monitoring solutions based on imported GPUs (e. g., the NVIDIA Jetson series) have drawbacks including high cost, high power consumption, and limited supply-chain autonomy. This paper presents the design and implementation of an intelligent pantograph condition monitoring system based on domestic RK3588 system-on-chip (SoC). This system employs a YOLOv8s object detection model, which is converted to an INT8 quantization model via the RKNN-Toolkit2 toolchain and deployed at the edge. By leveraging the RK3588's heterogeneous collaborative computing architecture (NPU, VPU, RGA, and multi-core CPU), the system performs low-latency real-time analysis of onboard high-definition video streams. Experimental results show that the system achieves an F1-score of up to 0.984 7 for six pantograph conditions and a processing rate of up to 88 FPS with 9-thread parallel optimization. Compared with mainstream solutions based on NVIDIA Jetson, the proposed system reduces board cost by at least 73% and power consumption by at least 33% while ensuring the required monitoring performance, providing an efficient and cost-effective solution with improved supply-chain autonomy for intelligent railway operation and maintenance.

title: Optimization of Face-Gait Person Identification Pipelines for Edge-Deployed Cognitive Agents
authors: Federico Boscolo; Grazia De Mola; Fabrizio Lamberti
venue: IEEE Annual International Computer Software and Applications Conference (COMPSAC)
abstract: Cognitive robotic systems require low-latency, reliable perception to support safe and context-aware interaction with humans. Multimodal biometrics (e.g., face and gait) improve robustness under real-world variations but the resulting pipelines are often too compute-intensive and memory-heavy for edge deployment. This paper explores the possibility of exploiting multimodal redundancy to enable aggressive optimization of person recognition stacks without excessive system-level degradation. We analyze a modular face+gait pipeline and apply architectural exploration together with post-training compression, namely quantization and pruning, targeting the dominant bottleneck (face recognition). Experiments on CASIA-B under a Rank-1 protocol over near-frontal views show that while face-only accuracy degrades significantly under compression (0.971 to 0.825), score-level fusion remains comparatively stable (0.986 to 0.966) while improving throughput from 49.8 to 75.2 FPS and reducing the deployed footprint from 295.2 MB to 111.9 MB. These results indicate that multimodal fusion can serve as a resilience mechanism, enabling lightweight and optimized perception modules for real-time cognitive agents.

title: Cooperative Augmented Reality: Displaying Occluded Vehicles using V2X Communications
authors: André Clérigo; Gonçalo Silva; Maximilian Schrapel; Pedro Rito; Susana Sargento; Alexey V. Vinel
abstract: As urban mobility increasingly integrates micromobility solutions such as bicycles, innovative road safety solutions have become a priority for these Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs). This work explores the use of Augmented Reality (AR) and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications to enhance cyclist safety at intersections with obstructed visibility. We propose an AR-based system that enables cyclists to visualize occluded vehicles using an 'X-ray' vision effect, leveraging real-time V2X messages and edge computing for low-latency interaction. The system architecture integrates multiple communication technologies, including 5G and ITS-G5, ensuring reliable transmission of road user data. To evaluate the system's feasibility, we conducted a real-world demonstration in the Aveiro Tech City Living Lab (ATCLL) platform using a Microsoft HoloLens 2 AR headset and an NVIDIA Jetson-based object detection pipeline. The system was tested in a real environment and results show that: (1) response time for total system latency falls within the 300 ms safety threshold defined by ETSI (which assures system safety); (2) the system operates on 3.75 FPS; and (3) increasing the video cameras's frame rate does not significantly affect resource and power consumption.

title: Landmark-aware visual localization for GNSS-denied UAV wind farm inspection via lifecycle binding and adaptive fusion
authors: Kai Zheng; Chao Deng; Maolin Xu; Chonghua Zhu; Enqi Xiao; Zhi Lu; Yujing Zhao; Wenquan Peng
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a lightweight landmark-aware visual localization framework intended as a backup localization subsystem for UAV inspection in GNSS-denied wind farms. The system utilizes wind turbine towers as natural semantic beacons and integrates YOLOv12s and BoT-SORT for real-time detection and robust tracking. Absolute pose estimation is achieved via a bbox-based 2.5-D image–altimeter geometry model, a landmark binding lifecycle management strategy (LBL), and an adaptive spatio-temporal weighted fusion algorithm (ASTW). In five repeated RflySim trials, the combined framework achieved a three-dimensional localization RMSE of $$8.33\pm 1.20$$ m compared with $$234.8\pm 42.3$$ m for the baseline, with end-to-end latency of approximately 200 ms per processed frame. In field validation at a 26-turbine wind farm, the algorithm ran online on a Jetson Xavier NX and independently generated visual position estimates without using RTK/GNSS data, achieving a three-dimensional RMSE of 24.95 m and a latency of 220 ms per processed frame. Because RTK/GNSS remained active for waypoint flight control and was recorded as ground truth, this experiment validates online GNSS-independent visual localization rather than closed-loop autonomous navigation under a physical GNSS outage. Because the field evaluation comprised one mission at one wind farm under favorable weather, the field result supports feasibility for area-level localization and coarse navigation assistance, but not yet high-precision close-range turbine inspection or broad generalization across sites and weather conditions.

title: AI-DRIVEN PREDICTIVE MAINTENANCE FOR HIGH-VOLTAGE X-RAY CT TUBES: A MANUFACTURING PERSPECTIVE
authors: Md Mahamudur Rahaman Shamim
abstract: High-voltage X-ray computed tomography (CT) tubes are critical components in advanced medical imaging, industrial inspection, and non-destructive evaluation systems. These vacuum-based devices operate under extreme electrical, thermal, and mechanical stress, making them highly susceptible to gradual degradation and sudden failure. Unplanned downtime of CT tubes can result in significant operational disruptions, financial loss, and safety risks. Traditional maintenance strategies—such as reactive or preventive maintenance—often fall short in anticipating complex failure mechanisms, especially in high-throughput environments. This study addresses this gap by proposing and validating a predictive maintenance framework powered by artificial intelligence (AI) and designed specifically for high-voltage CT tube systems within industrial manufacturing contexts. The research adopted a hybrid experimental-computational methodology, combining simulated sensor data with real-world failure records to develop and evaluate machine learning and deep learning models. A dataset comprising 18,000 multivariate sensor sequences—including filament current, cathode temperature, vacuum pressure, and rotor vibration—was used to train five predictive models: random forest, support vector machine (SVM), convolutional neural network (CNN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and autoencoder-based anomaly detection. Feature extraction was performed using signal processing techniques, and model performance was assessed using accuracy, F1-score, remaining useful life (RUL) prediction error, and inference latency under real-time constraints. Additionally, a Raspberry Pi-based edge computing prototype was developed to validate real-time deployment feasibility, and a centralized monitoring dashboard was created to visualize health status and facilitate technician interaction. Results showed that LSTM models outperformed other algorithms in temporal degradation forecasting, achieving a ±5% error in RUL estimation and offering a 24–48 hour predictive lead time. Multisensor data fusion significantly improved detection accuracy and model stability across diverse operating scenarios. The autoencoder demonstrated exceptional performance in detecting novel and rare fault patterns without prior labeling, with a 96% detection rate and low false positive incidence. Edge deployment tests confirmed low-latency model inference suitable for real-time applications, while dashboard integration improved decision-making efficiency and technician trust in AI outputs. Overall, the proposed framework enabled proactive intervention, reduced maintenance overhead, and extended CT tube operational uptime. These findings highlight the strategic value of AI-enhanced predictive maintenance in optimizing industrial reliability, aligning with the broader goals of Industry 4.0 and smart manufacturing ecosystems.

title: AI-Powered Baby Monitoring System Using Computer Vision and Real-Time Anomaly Detection
authors: Ameena Asmi P K; Aysha Minha C H; Kadeeja Amna K; Rasha V P
venue: IEEE International Conference on Recent Advances in Electronics, Communication, Computing, Automation and Power (RECCAP)
abstract: Parents constantly worry about infant safety, especially during sleep or when they cannot supervise. Traditional baby monitors stream video without understanding the content, requiring ongoing human attention. This paper introduces a camera-based monitoring system that automatically detects dangerous situations for infants in real time. Our system uses facial recognition to confirm the baby’s presence and analyzes body position through pose estimation. It sends instant alerts to the parent’s mobile device when it detects risky behaviors, such as face-down sleeping or climbing. The system runs on NVIDIA Jetson Nano for low-latency edge processing and works in both daylight and nighttime. Testing showed over 90 percent accuracy in detecting hazardous positions while keeping response times under one second. Parents receive automated alerts about dangers instead of having to watch video continuously.

title: Data Collection, Organization, and Privacy-Preserving Preparation for Edge-Based LLMs in Legal Text Analytics
authors: Asimina Dimara; Konstantinos Kotis; Alexios Papaioannou; Stamatis Chatzistamatis; Nikolaos Evangeliou; Chrysaphis Nathanailidis; George E. Tsekouras
venue: International Conference on Electrical, Computer, Communications and Mechatronics Engineering (ICECCME)
abstract: Providing fairness and privacy in automated legal text processing is an essential issue, especially with the increasing usage of Large Language Models (LLMs), in sensitive public sector applications. This paper presents a modular edge native domain-specific architecture for legal document processing that avoids cloud infrastructure and external APIs. The system combines local ingestion, semantic embedding, and retrievalaugmented generation to empower autonomous agents for applications such as bias detection and clause summarization. Inference is done exclusively on-device by a 4-bit quantized LLaMA model run by CPU-only runtimes. Tested on the CLEAR-Bias benchmark, the system gets $92 \%$ prompt relevance and $90 \%$ output coherence, inference latency below 6.5 s, and memory usage below 5.5 GB. These findings validate the effectiveness of privacy-preserving, regulation-conforming legal NLP in constrained environments.

title: Deploying Real-Time Speech Recognition on ESP32 Using TinyML and Edge Impulse
authors: Manuel González; Sebastián Gutiérrez; Ricardo Espinosa; Hiram Ponce-Espinosa
venue: Communications in computer and information science

title: AI-Integrated Smart Campus Framework: Intelligent Attendance, Security, and Student Support Using Edge Vision and NLP Systems
authors: Syeda Khubtiya Khanum A; K B Naveen; B. N. Shobha; S B Manoj Kumar; M B Anandaraju; Manjunatha G
venue: International Conference on Emerging Research in Smart Electronics and Machine Informatics (ECMI)
abstract: AI-integrated smart campuses are redefining institutional efficiency by unifying real-time attendance automation, intelligent security monitoring, and student support services through advanced edge vision and natural language processing (NLP) systems. This paper presents a comprehensive AIdriven smart campus framework designed to enhance academic operations, safety, and student-faculty interaction. The proposed system leverages lightweight CNN and Vision Transformer models deployed on edge devices for facebased attendance and real- time surveillance analytics, achieving 96.8% detection accuracy with sub-$\mathbf{4 5}$ms inference latency. A multimodal NLP-powered student support chatbot, trained using retrieval-augmented responses, demonstrates$\mathbf{9 2. 4 \%}$intent classification accuracy and reduces query resolution time by$\mathbf{6 1 \%}$. Real-world deployment results show improvements in attendance efficiency (+38%), incident detection responsiveness (+47%), and faculty workload reduction ($+29 \%$) compared to traditional systems. While the framework delivers strong gains in accuracy, speed, and autonomy, challenges remain in large-scale edge deployment, model generalization across illumination conditions, and integration with legacy campus management platforms. Future work will focus on expanding sensor fusion for environmental monitoring, developing campus- wide digital twins, and implementing privacy-preserving federated learning for secure AI-driven campus governance.

title: Democratizing Truth: Optimizing Transformer Models for Client-Side Misinformation Detection in Resource-Constrained Environments
authors: Shambhavi Singh
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The exponential proliferation of digital misinformation presents a critical challenge for information integrity, particularly in developing regions where network latency, data costs, and intermittent connectivity prohibit reliance on cloud-based verification systems. While Large Language Models (LLMs) and Transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT) offer state-of-the-art performance in automated fact-checking, their significant memory footprint (>400 MB) and computational latency render them unsuitable for client-side deployment on consumer hardware. This study addresses this "Digital Divide" by proposing a lightweight, offline-capable architecture for real-time misinformation detection. Leveraging the LIAR dataset, I fine-tuned a DistilBERT model and engineered a compression pipeline utilizing Dynamic Quantization (INT8) and ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) Runtime Optimization. The approach achieved a 74.8% reduction in model size (from 255.45 MB to 64.45 MB), successfully crossing the critical 100 MB threshold required for browser extension deployment. Furthermore, inference latency on standard CPU hardware was reduced by 55.2% (from 52.73 ms to 23.58 ms), establishing feasibility for synchronous user interaction. These results demonstrate that complex Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks can be democratized for edge deployment, enabling privacy-preserving, accessible AI safety tools in regions with limited connectivity.

title: Ανάπτυξη ολοκληρωμένου συστήματος επιτήρησης με χρήση αυτόνομων UAV μέσω edge computing, δικτυακής ασφάλειας και ενσωματωμένης τεχνητής νοημοσύνης
authors: Πασχάλης Ι. Μοσχογιάννης
venue: University of Thessaly Institutional Repository (University of Thessaly)
abstract: This master's thesis presents the design, implementation, and validation of an integrated surveillance system built on a heterogeneous swarm of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs).The architecture is engineered for autonomous, real-time operation in infrastructure-denied environments by combining edge intelligence with a resilient, self-organizing communication fabric.A leader-follower paradigm allocates global target acquisition to a GPU-equipped leader, while lighter followers provide complementary viewpoints and serve as mesh relays.The system's flight stack interfaces natively with ROS 2 via PX4's uXRCE-DDS client, enabling direct offboard control through the ROS 2 graph.Perception is executed entirely at the edge: the leader runs YOLOv5s accelerated with NVIDIA TensorRT, while followers use an optimized YOLOv5n on a Rockchip NPU via the RKNN toolkit.To ensure transport isolation, annotated video previews are written to V4L2 loopback devices and streamed by independent sidecar daemons using an HEVC/SRT pipeline.The communications backbone is a two-layer mesh: BATMAN-adv at Layer 2 provides a flat broadcast domain for seamless ROS 2 DDS discovery, while Babel at Layer 3 reconnects segmented network clusters.The complete system was validated end-to-end in high-fidelity Gazebo SITL and on hardware benches.The results demonstrate reliable multi-hop ROS 2 operation, stable offboard control loops, and low-latency video streaming, confirming the architecture's viability for persistent, autonomous surveillance missions.

title: SqueezeNetVLAD: High-speed power and memory efficient GPS less accurate network model for visual place recognition on the edge
authors: Chandrajit Pal; Pratibha Verma; H R Rohit; Dubacharla Gyaneshwar; Sumohana S. Channappayya; Amit Acharyya
abstract: Visual place recognition (VPR) provides the ability for a machine to recognise any given place if it has been visited before by utilising visual graphics data. Classical handcrafted feature extraction doesn’t seem to perform well under varying environmental conditions, which is where the convolutional neural networks with their state-of-the-art performance act as a substitute however at the cost of an increased computational complexity making it difficult to port into resource-constrained edge devices like tiny robots, drones etc. This motivated us to propose an optimal NetVLAD network algorithm consisting of an optimised and efficient feature extraction base network performing feature extraction while satisfying both a given constraint of accuracy and the resource budget of a target implementation platform. Both the accuracy, which is marginally better, the achieved model size reduction is better by 17% and a nominal power reduction by 5% w.r.t the SOTA models. Also developed a customised CUDA kernel that dynamically compares the pair of query image feature vectors to the descriptor vectors of the already stored gallery image datasets in parallel utilising the maximum available tensor cores achieving hard-real time performance at 62.5 fps with input videos tested on the Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX platform.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Classification of Human Activities from mmWave Radar Point Clouds
authors: Ethem Şekerci; Ayhan Küçükmanіşa
venue: International Conference on Electronics, Computers and Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
abstract: This paper presents a real time human activity classification system using three dimensional point clouds produced by millimeter wave radar and a PointNet based deep learning model. A Texas Instruments IWR6843ISK radar operating between 60 and 64 GHz was used to collect data from 10 subjects, including 5 female and 5 male participants, performing five distinct gestures: waist bending, arm flapping, arm swinging, forward bending, and lateral bending. Data were recorded through Robot Operating System 2, converted into sliding window segments of 500 points with a stride of 250 points, quality filtered, and normalized before being fed to a shared multilayer perceptron and global max pooling classifier. The final curated dataset contains 4,155 segments split into 3,324 training samples and 831 test samples. The model achieves 98 percent test accuracy and a macro F1 score of zero point ninety seven. In addition to a contextual comparison with literature baselines, an in house RadHAR reproduction on the same dataset reached 93 percent accuracy, confirming the advantage of direct raw point processing for this dataset. Real time inference runs at approximately 35 frames per second on Jetson Nano and approximately 25 frames per second on Raspberry Pi 4, demonstrating suitability for embedded and contactless monitoring in smart living, rehabilitation, and human machine interaction scenarios.

title: IoT-Enabled deep learning for monitoring physical responses in biological systems
authors: Feruza Yashieva; Akhmedova Sarvinoz; Dulan Eshonqulov; Nodira Khudoyberdiyeva; Farrukh Narzullaev
abstract: An IoT-enabled, multimodal sensing and deep-learning framework is introduced for monitoring physiological responses of biological preparations subjected to controlled photostimulation, mild heating, and low-intensity electromagnetic exposure. A compact node acquires synchronized optical, thermal, and electromagnetic channels and streams timestamped packets to an edge-cloud pipeline. On-device temporal convolutional networks perform real-time event detection, while a transformer-based regressor estimates key biophysical parameters-photoreaction latency, thermal sensitivity, and electromagnetic-induced response amplitude. Data efficiency and robustness are enhanced through self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled sequences and a physics-aware loss that enforces monotonic trends and plausible parameter bounds. Predictive uncertainty is quantified with lightweight model ensembles to obtain calibrated decision thresholds suitable for safety-critical operation. In benchtop evaluations, the framework reduces parameter mean-absolute-error by 12-18% and increases event-detection area-under-the-receiver-operating-characteristic by 0.07-0.12 relative to strong baselines. End-to-end inference on an embedded CPU achieves <10 ms latency at <2 W power, supporting closed-loop experimentation. These results indicate that coupling synchronized IoT sensing with physics-informed deep models yields accurate, low-latency, and energy-aware monitoring appropriate for bio-lab workflows operating under thermal and electromagnetic safety constraints.

title: Federated Data Analytics Framework for Distributed Sound Source Localization Using Wireless Microphone Networks and TinyViT Learning
authors: Robert Gajić
abstract: Wireless microphone node arrays offer a flexible sensing layer for acoustic monitoring, emergency perception, conference-room interaction, and mobile robot audition, but their localization accuracy is often affected by non-identical node placement, packet-level instability, and acoustic-domain non-IID data. This paper proposes an improved FedProx-TinyViT model for distributed sound source localization in wireless microphone node arrays. Multichannel short-time spectra, phase-difference cues, and node confidence descriptors are transformed into compact acoustic tokens, and a TinyViT backbone with local-window attention and cross-node fusion is trained through FedProx under heterogeneous reverberation and signal-to-noise conditions. A simulated and replayed wireless array dataset with 8 node layouts, 12 source azimuths, 5 reverberation settings, and 6 noise conditions was used for evaluation. Compared with centralized CNN, local TinyViT, FedAvg-TinyViT, and FedNova-TinyViT baselines, the proposed model achieved a mean angular error of 3.84 degrees, a within-5-degree localization rate of 91.6%, a 38.7% reduction in uplink payload, and 18.4 ms edge inference latency on an ARM-class node. Under 20% packet loss, the method obtained a mean error of 5.21 degrees, whereas FedAvg-TinyViT reached 7.46 degrees. These results indicate that proximal federated optimization and lightweight attention can jointly improve accuracy, communication efficiency, and deployment tolerance for distributed acoustic localization.

title: CNN-assisted automated order selection for SARIMAX in online ship roll prediction
authors: Hamed Majidiyan; Hossein Enshaei; Damon Howe
abstract: Autonomous ships require reliable response-prediction units to enhance safety and decision-making, with roll forecasting central to stability control and propulsion efficiency. In this study, we develop a SARIMAX-based roll predictor that treats ship speed as an exogenous input and employs a lightweight CNN to determine the orders directly from ACF/PACF images, thereby eliminating iterative AIC/BIC sweeps. The pipeline is designed for online/edge deployment, offering low-latency training and inference suitable for modest onboard hardware. Granger-causality analyses across varied operating scenarios confirm that speed materially improves roll predictability. Under matched 200-s windows, the approach reduces order-selection time by ∼92 % (sub-second versus >14 s) and delivers better forecast accuracy than classical SARIMA and deep-learning baselines (LSTM, GRU, TCN, Transformer). CPU-only timing is reported for fairness, with GPU used solely for CNN training. Experiments spanning 36 simulator runs (routes/speeds/sea states) and open-source model-test cases (KCS, KVLCC) demonstrate scalability and robustness of the proposed framework. The method operates on short sliding windows and does not rely on long historical logs, enabling cold-start deployment in intermittently connected settings. • Proposes an engineering-oriented SARIMAX-CNN framework for real-time prediction of ship roll motion. • Presents a scalable order identification method using ACF/PACF image classification with over 87,000 pre-trained patterns. • Enables computationally efficient forecasting with 92 % runtime reduction, supporting Industry 4.0 in smart ship systems.

title: Lightweight Multiscale Perception and Global Context Guidance Network for Crowd Counting in Congested Scene
authors: Xiaojian Hu; Chenxi Lin
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Accurate measurement of crowd density plays a critical role in public safety and intelligent transportation systems. In practical scenarios, cameras and embedded devices serve as essential instruments for real-time measurement. However, the discrepancy between the heavy network architecture frequently utilized for high-precision counting tasks and the constrained computational resource inherent in edge device has emerged as a significant challenge. In order to address this challenge, we propose an effective encoder-decoder based network, named lightweight multiscale perception and global context guidance network. Specifically, lightweight MobileOne network is applied as backbone for efficient feature extraction. Adaptive large kernel attention module is proposed for multiscale spatial hierarchy relationship extraction. Global context guidance module is designed for the fusion of multi-level features, allowing the extraction of effective global information from high-level feature to propagate to low-level feature. Experiments on four crowd counting datasets demonstrate that the proposed model is able to achieve comparable counting performance while maintaining small model size and low inference latency. The proposed model is deployed on Nvidia Jetson Nano and applied in edge density estimation of non-motorized transportation participants in Nanjing, providing important data foundation for traffic signal timing optimization.

title: UDW: A Dataset For Automated Monitoring Of Cargo-Handling During Sling-Load Operations
authors: Marvin Brenner; Peter Stütz
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotic Computing (IRC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles can automate transportation of construction materials and supplies to remote locations. Current operations are performed by manned helicopter crews as the cargo is typically attached with an external sling-load hook and its placement requires precise cooperation between pilot and members on the ground. To ensure the safety of comparable operations with an unmanned rotorcraft, it shall automatically assess the object composition on the ground like a human pilot. Given the limited amount of video data depicting operations in the field from a top-view perspective, a novel dataset of interactions between ground crew, pilot and payload is presented. It includes over 17,000 manual annotations for the aerial object detection of people, ground vehicles, various payloads and cargo hooks. In addition, the crew members are labelled with pose attributes to infer additional state information in the same inference step. Despite the high variation in perspective, a trained detection transformer reached a validation mAP50 of$80.4 \% $, a recall of$76.4\% $at an inference latency of$50\ ms$on a NVIDIA Jetson Orin. The dataset is made publicy available under the following link: https://universe.roboflow.com/lft/upsidedownwash.

title: Quantized SNNs for Smart Grid Fault Detection
authors: Benjamin Agyekum; Daniel Seffah-Duodu; AGYAPONG GLORIA
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Quantized Event-Driven Spiking Neural Network, named Q-GridSNN, for real-time smart grid fault detection under noisy, dynamic, and resource-constrained operating conditions. The study addresses the computational burden of conventional deep learning models deployed for transmission-line and distribution-network fault diagnosis by combining spike-based temporal encoding, quantization-aware training, adaptive membrane-potential scaling, and lightweight edge inference. Voltage, current, phasor measurement unit signals, and derived symmetrical components are encoded into sparse spike trains using latency-rate hybrid coding, allowing the model to capture transient fault signatures with reduced switching activity. The proposed Q-GridSNN is benchmarked against Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, Graph Neural Network, full-precision SNN, and baseline Quantized SNN models. Evaluation is performed using multiclass fault conditions, including line-to-ground, line-to-line, double-line-to-ground, three-phase faults, high-impedance faults, and normal operating states. Comparative results show that Q-GridSNN achieves superior performance, with a projected accuracy of 99.31%, precision of 99.18%, recall of 98.96%, F1-score of 99.07%, and fault localization error below 0.42 km. The model also reduces inference latency to 2.6 ms and lowers estimated energy consumption by 58.4% compared with full-precision SNN and by 71.2% compared with CNN-LSTM. Graphical analysis using confusion matrices, ROC curves, precision-recall curves, latency-energy trade-off plots, and quantization sensitivity graphs confirms that the proposed model preserves diagnostic accuracy while substantially improving computational efficiency. The findings demonstrate that quantized SNNs can provide a practical pathway for intelligent, low-power, and fast fault detection in smart grids, especially for edge-based protection relays, distributed substations, and cyber-physical power-system monitoring platforms.

title: A Cloud–Edge Collaborative Enabling Architecture Based on a Heterogeneous Embedded Platform
authors: Dongqi Han; Dongming Yuan; Yuan'an Liu
venue: International Conference on Big Data, Communication Technology and Computer Applications (BDCTA)
abstract: As the application of artificial intelligence in edge scenarios becomes increasingly widespread, cloud-edge collaborative computing has become a new solution for achieving low latency and reliable intelligent services. However, edge devices are limited by size, energy consumption, and limited computing resources, while tightly coupled embedded platforms lack flexibility and scalability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a cloud-edge collaborative support architecture based on heterogeneous embedded platforms. At the architectural level, a lightweight cloud-edge framework is designed to support the integration and coordination of heterogeneous edge computing resources. At the hardware level, a modular and multi-domain heterogeneous embedded platform is implemented, which realizes flexible configuration and upgrade of CPUs, NPUs, and FPGAs computing units through standardized interfaces. The proposed architecture can achieve adaptive collaboration among the cloud, edge, and device layers under different network conditions and task requirements. Experimental results show that the proposed solution has improved performance in edge inference, scalability, and operational flexibility, providing a new practical solution for autonomous edge computing clusters and intelligent base station systems.

title: Low-level Optimizations for Faster Mobile Deep Learning Inference Frameworks
authors: Mathieu Febvay
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
abstract: Over the last ten years, we have seen a strong progression of technology around smartphones. Each new generation acquires capabilities that significantly increase performance. On the other hand, several deep learning tools are offered today by the giants of the net for mobile, embedded devices and IoT. The proposed libraries allow a machine learning inference on the device with low latency. They provide pre-trained models, but one can also use one's own models and run them on mobile, embedded or microcontroller devices. Lack of privacy, poor Internet connectivity and high cost of cloud platform let on-device inference became popular through app developers but there are more significant challenges especially for real-time tasks like augmented reality or autonomous driving. This PhD research aims at providing a path for developers to help them choose the best methods and tools to do real-time inference on mobile devices. In this paper, we present the performance benchmark of four popular open-source deep learning inference frameworks used on mobile devices on three different convolutional neural network models. We focus our work on image classification process and particularly on validation image bank of ImageNet 2012 dataset. We try to answer three questions : How does a framework influence model prediction and latency - Why some frameworks are better in terms of latency/accuracy than others with the same model - And what are the difficulties to implement these frameworks inside a mobile application - Our first findings demonstrate that low-level software implementations chosen in frameworks, model conversion steps and parameters set in the framework have a big impact on performance and accuracy.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Agriculture: Advancing Climate-Resilient Crop Production through Integrated Pest and Disease Detection
authors: Yasir Rasheed; Muhammad Shahhan; Hamza Sheraz; Muhammad Rasheed Ahmad
venue: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
abstract: Anthropogenic climate change is drastically shifting insect pest dynamics, triggering premature population outbreaks, expanding species geographical ranges, and destabilizing global agroecosystems. Conventional crop protection relies on broad-spectrum broadcast chemical applications that cause severe ecotoxicological harm to non-target fauna—such as honeybee pollinators (Apis mellifera), predatory ladybird beetles (Coccinella septempunctata), green lacewings (Chrysoperla carnea), and egg parasitoids (Trichogramma chilonis). This study presents and empirically validates the Synergistic Bio-AI Entomological Framework (SBAEF), bridging fundamental ecological entomology with digital precision tools (YOLOv8 vision models, multispectral edge computing, autonomous variable-rate micro-actuation) in compliance with FAO ISPM (3, 6, 14) and EPPO PP1 phytosanitary guidelines. Across multi-crop field trials (tomato and cotton) over two consecutive seasons (2024–2025; n = 48 experimental plots), AI-guided micro-spot applications reduced chemical active ingredient volume by 72.4% compared to conventional broadcast spraying (p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 4.12). Non-target beneficial survival was preserved: Apis mellifera survival reached 96.8% [95% CI: 95.2–98.4%] (vs. 12.3% under broadcast), and Trichogramma chilonis emergence reached 86.7% [95% CI: 84.1–89.3%] (vs. 18.5%). Computer vision validation demonstrated a Mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 95.6% for target pests and 93.8% for beneficial insects at an edge-inference latency of 11.4 ms/frame. Crop yields under AI-IPM increased by 3.8% over conventional broadcast (p = 0.012), proving that precision micro-actuation stabilizes food production while restoring biological control.

title: Design and implementation of an embedded system for traffic sign detection and recognition system
authors: Manish Nandy; Dhablia Dharmesh Kirit
abstract: The need for precise and computationally effective traffic sign detecting systems has grown as autonomous driving technology has advanced. However, solving crucial accuracy and processing speed problems is necessary to get such a system to a deployable state. RetinaNet, a focal loss-based single-stage object detector, is utilised to balance processing speed and accuracy because it addresses the single-stage detector’s class imbalance issue and is therefore appropriate for traffic sign detection (TSD). Given the progress being made in next-generation transportation systems and the increasing need for autonomous vehicles, it is imperative that a system be put in place that can recognise traffic signs quickly and precisely. The three key elements of a traffic sign recognition system that are the focus of this work are detection, tracking, and classification. In order to reduce the number of accidents, ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance System) for driverless cars must include a strong traffic sign recognition system. The widely used datasets for traffic sign recognition systems are described in this article, together with an analysis of their salient characteristics, the deep learning models that were utilised, and a comparative study of the different models. Moreover, the main research works up to this point are summarised and discussed, with a focus on CNNs and their use in traffic sign identification. The third method is building a model for traffic sign detection (TSD) using a one-stage object detection framework that uses YOLOv5m. In particular, this model is tuned for real-time inference on the Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX embedded device.
