title: HW/SW Development of Cloud-RAN in 3D Networks: Computational and Energy Resources for Splitting Options
authors: Stefano Bonafini; Claudio Sacchi; Fabrizio Granelli; Sisay Tadesse Arzo; Michael Devetsikiotis; Koteswararao Kondepu
abstract: The continuous increase in demanding for availability and ultra-reliability of low-latency and broadband wireless connections is instigating further research in the standardization of next-generation mobile systems. 6G networks, among other benefits, should offer global ubiquitous mobility thanks to the utilization of the Space segment as an intelligent yet autonomous ecosystem. In this framework, multi-layered networks will take charge of providing connectivity by implementing Cloud-Radio Access Network (C-RAN) functionalities on heterogeneous nodes distributed over aerial and orbital segments. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), High-Altitude Plat-forms (HAPs), and small satellites compose the Space ecosystem encompassing the 3D networks. Recently, a lot of interest has been raised about splitting operations to distribute baseband processing functionalities among such nodes to balance the computational load and reduce the power consumption. This work focuses on the hardware development of C-RAN physical (PHY-) layer operations to derive their computational and energy demand. More in detail, the 5G Downlink Shared Channel (DLSCH) and the Physical Downlink Shared Channel (PDSCH) are first simulated in MATLAB environment to evaluate the variation of computational load depending on the selected splitting options and number of antennas available at transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) side. Then, the PHY-layer processing chain is software-implemented and the various splitting options are tested on low-cost processors, such as Raspberry Pi (RP) 3B+ and 4B. By overclocking the RPs, we compute the execution time and we derive the instruction count (IC) per program for each considered splitting option so to achieve the mega instructions per second (MIPS) for the expected processing time. Finally, by comparing the performance achieved by the employed RPs with that of Nvidia Jetson Nano (JN) processor used as benchmark, we shall discuss about size, weight, power and cost (SWaP-C) metrics related to the UAV payload design.

title: Edge-Optimized Facial Emotion Recognition: A High-Performance Hybrid Mobilenetv2-Vit Model
authors: Susmith Rajendra Barigidad
venue: International Journal of AI BigData Computational and Management Studies
abstract: Computer vision applications span various fields including healthcare, security, autonomous vehicles, and augmented reality, enabling machines to interpret and analyze visual data. Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) is a subclass of healthcare applications that leverages computer vision to analyze and interpret human emotions from facial expressions. Facial emotion recognition also plays a vital role in human-computer interaction, with applications in security, and affective computing. This study suggests a deep learning (DL) based hybrid model integrating MobileNetV2 for efficient feature extraction and a Vision Transformer (ViT) for capturing global facial dependencies. The dataset obtained from Kaggle is used for training, which is then preprocessed and augmented. The trained model is deployed on a smartphone as an edge device, enabling real-time emotion recognition with improved privacy, low latency, and minimal computational overhead. During testing, facial images captured by the smartphone are preprocessed using the Haar Cascade algorithm before being fed into the model for classification. Performance evaluation using accuracy, recall, precision and F1-score demonstrates a high classification accuracy of 98.51%, confirming the model’s effectiveness. The proposed approach enhances on-device FER capabilities, making it a promising solution for emotion-aware applications in mobile healthcare and intelligent human-computer interactions

title: RT-SROD: Real-Time Suspicious Roadside Object Detection with a CNN–ViT Hybrid
authors: Rithick Roshan S; Abirami; A Jenefa
venue: International Conference of Advances in Engineering and Computing Technologies for Sustainable Development (AECTSD)
abstract: Roadside surveillance must identify suspicious objects with speed and reliability to support timely public safety responses. Illumination variation, motion blur, and video compression complicate accurate real-time detection. This work pursues two goals in tandem: high accuracy and low latency under diverse CCTV conditions. A central difficulty is to sustain precise localization and well-calibrated decisions in low light, fog or haze, and streaming compression. Pure CNN detectors provide strong local texture cues and high throughput but struggle with long-range context and domain shifts. Transformer-only detectors capture global relationships yet often incur higher latency and unstable small-object localization. We present a cross-attentional CNN–Vision Transformer hybrid that fuses convolutional features with global token context for scale-aware, robust detection. An optimized TensorRT FP16 deployment preserves real-time throughput while standardizing pre/post-processing across models. Experiments use a scene-stratified corpus of 12,000 surveillance frames with 20,890 annotated instances across five classes (train/val/test: 8,500/1,500/2,000). Resolutions span 720–2160px (median 1080p), with splits preventing camera-stream leakage. The proposed model achieves mAP@0.50 = 92.3, mAP@0.50:0.95 = 63.4, and F1 = 90.9 at 45 FPS with 22.2ms latency (640×640), outperforming YOLOv8-s by +3.2/+5.4 percentage points. Robustness drops remain within single digits under adverse conditions, including low light at −8.9 percentage points and fog or haze at −8.0 percentage points. Probabilistic calibration performs very well, with an expected calibration error of 0.032. These transfer learning results indicate that, such an integration of both cross-attentional mechanisms between convolutional and transformer-based cues shows better accuracy while preserving practically acceptable speedups for roadside surveillance. It is seen that performance is stable under various scene types, and that the quality under the compression process is maintained, which means robustness.

title: Smart Wearable for Vital Tracking and Alerts
authors: Ms Saranya S 1, Gurpreet Singh 2, Sahil Kumar 3, Gagandeep Singh 4, Digantik Mukherjee 5
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The increasing demand for ongoing, remote health monitoring for people with chronic illnesses and aging populations calls for a change from passive data collecting to intelligent, proactive systems [1], [2]. Real-time, on-device predictive analytics, reliable fall detection, and an integrated, closed-loop emergency response system that connects users to emergency medical assistance are frequently absent from current commercial wearables. We introduce an integrated wearable system with an ADXL345 accelerometer for fall detection and a MAX30102 sensor for heart rate and SpO2 monitoring, all based on an ESP32 microcontroller. The solution uses an on-device AI model that is lightweight and tuned with TensorFlow Lite to detect anomalies in physiological data in real time. The system reliably detects abnormalities in vital signs and shows great efficacy in differentiating falls from activities of daily living (ADLs). Importantly, it automatically retrieves the user’s GPS coordinates and uses the Google Maps API to find local medical institutions, achieving an end-to-end emergency alert latency of less than 5 seconds. Real-time, on-device predictive analytics, reliable fall detection, and an integrated, closed-loop emergency response system that connects users to emergency medical assistance are freq By bridging the crucial gap between health anomaly detection and practical emergency intervention, our work offers a low-latency, energy-efficient, privacy-preserving approach that improves patient safety and autonomy

title: Machine Learning-Based Predictive Maintenance Framework for Rotating Equipment in Process Industries
authors: Dr. K. Sujatha
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a paradigm-shifting approach to asset lifecycle management in process industries, promising significant reductions in unplanned downtime, maintenance costs, and safety-related incidents relative to conventional schedule-based and condition-based strategies. The proliferation of industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensors, edge computing platforms, and cloud-based data pipelines has made large-scale vibration, temperature, acoustic emission, and operational parameter data routinely available for machine learning (ML) model development. However, translating raw time-series sensor data into actionable fault prognostics remains a non-trivial engineering challenge, encompassing signal preprocessing, feature extraction in time, frequency, and time-frequency domains, class imbalance handling, cross-machine generalisation, and operational deployment under real-time latency constraints. This study presents a comprehensive ML-based predictive maintenance framework evaluated on rotating equipment — specifically centrifugal pumps, induction motors, and gearboxes — instrumented with triaxial accelerometers, thermocouples, and current sensors across three process plant sites in Northern India. Five ML algorithms are benchmarked: Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and a proposed hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture. Feature importance analysis using SHAP values identifies the ten most predictive features across fault types. A cost-benefit model quantifies maintenance savings relative to a baseline reactive maintenance regime. The CNN-LSTM hybrid achieves the highest macro-F1 score of 0.923 across seven fault classes — including bearing inner/outer race faults, impeller cavitation, rotor imbalance, and gear tooth spalling — outperforming standalone LSTM (0.891) and Random Forest (0.874). SHAP analysis reveals that RMS acceleration in the 1-3× running speed band, kurtosis of the envelope spectrum, and thermal gradient rate are the three dominant predictive features across all equipment types. Deployment on an edge computing node (Raspberry Pi 4 with NVIDIA Jetson inference) achieves inference latency of 47 ms per prediction cycle — within the 100 ms real-time threshold required by the plant SCADA system. The cost-benefit model projects annual savings of ₹18.6 lakhs per monitored asset, yielding payback period of 14 months on sensor and software investment

title: The critical paradigm shifts for next-generation AI-empowered smart wearable devices
authors: Chengzu Li; Junxiong Zhang; Guangliang Tian; Gui Yang; Xinyang He
abstract: Despite rapid progress in health monitoring, many smart wearable devices still function primarily as passive sensing-and-logging platforms. Their performance is constrained by fixed hardware configurations and cloud-centric analytics pipelines. As a result, they often fail to deliver real-time responses to user intent and rarely support closed-loop physical intervention. This perspective argues that enabling embodied intelligence in wearables requires three paradigm shifts. First, wearables should transition from closed, integrated hardware to open, modular computing architectures that can accommodate evolving on-device artificial intelligence (AI) demands. Second, cloud-dependent inference should be replaced, where appropriate, by ultra-low-latency edge intelligence to support millisecond-scale prediction and control. Third, devices should evolve from passive information feedback to active physical intervention supported by human-in-the-loop optimization. Together, these shifts may reshape the human–machine relationship by moving wearables from external tools toward digital partners that operate under explicit user intent and safety constraints.

title: Smart Cattle Behavior Sensing with Embedded Vision and TinyML at the Edge
authors: Jazzie R. Jao; Edgar A. Vallar; Ibrahim A. Hameed
venue: International Electronic Conference on Sensors and Applications (ECSA)
abstract: Accurate real-time monitoring of cattle behavior is essential for enabling data-driven decision-making in precision livestock farming. However, existing monitoring solutions often rely on cloud-based processing or high-power hardware, which are impractical for deployment in remote or low-infrastructure agricultural environments. There is a critical need for low-cost, energy-efficient, and autonomous sensing systems capable of operating independently at the edge. This paper presents a compact, sensor-integrated system for real-time cattle behavior monitoring using an embedded vision sensor and a TinyML-based inference pipeline. The system is designed for low-power deployment in field conditions and integrates the OV2640 image sensor with the Sipeed Maixduino platform, which features the Kendryte K210 RISC-V processor and an on-chip neural network accelerator (KPU). The platform supports fully on-device classification of cattle postures using a quantized convolutional neural network trained on the publicly available cattle behavior dataset, covering standing and lying behavioral states. Sensor data is captured via the onboard camera and preprocessed in real time to meet model input specifications. The trained model is quantized and converted into a K210-compatible. kmodel using the NNCase toolchain, and deployed using MaixPy firmware. System performance was evaluated based on inference latency, classification accuracy, memory usage, and energy efficiency. Results demonstrate that the proposed TinyML-enabled system can accurately classify cattle behaviors in real time while operating within the constraints of a low-power, embedded platform, making it a viable solution for smart livestock monitoring in remote or under-resourced environments.

title: Energy-efficient deep learning-based vibration monitoring on parallel ultra-low-power microcontrollers
authors: Amirhossein Kiamarzi; Federica Zonzini; Amirhossein Moallemi; Davide Rossi; Giuseppe Tagliavini
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) through vibration analysis is essential for ensuring safety, reliability, and minimized maintenance costs in sensor-connected environments. Realizing this at the extreme edge, directly on sensor nodes, requires advanced data analytics, ultra-energy-efficient hardware, and high-fidelity datasets. This paper addresses these challenges by developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based deep learning framework for vibration-based structural health monitoring tailored to resource-constrained devices. We present a benchmarking dataset for vibration SHM, encompassing nine abnormal conditions that capture narrowband structural anomalies. Leveraging this dataset, we design supervised and unsupervised deep-learning models, integrating a system identification (SysId) preprocessing stage to derive structurally informed features that enhance model input quality. This improves algorithmic results while boosting hardware performances. These models are deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power microcontroller with dedicated hardware acceleration. Our unsupervised anomaly detectors deliver 89.90 percent (%) accuracy, 4.1 percentage points higher than the state-of-the-art attention-based baseline, favoring recall and missed-detection reduction at the cost of a higher false-alarm rate while consuming 13 microjoules (µJ) in low-power mode and requiring 370 microseconds (µs) in high-performance mode. This marks one of the first experimental validations of unsupervised on-device vibration diagnostics. Supervised counterparts achieve 96.06 % binary and 91.5 % multiclass accuracy, rivaling Residual Network (ResNet) with 1 5 . 8 × fewer parameters, at less than 235 µJ and not more than 6.3 ms (ms) inference. Relative to existing edge implementations, our approach is one to three orders of magnitude more energy-efficient and two orders faster, unlocking AI-enabled autonomous, low-latency predictive maintenance for large-scale distributed infrastructure monitoring.

title: Edge AI-enabled dynamic power factor correction using TinyML, blockchain and IoT for real-time smart grid optimization and industrial applications
authors: Ch. Gochhayat Prakash; Md Afam; Alam Sk Md Tanvir; K. Mallick Gaurav; Sarker Krishna; Paramanik Sayan
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive design and implementation of an AI-enabled Smart Power Factor Correction (PFC) System that integrates advanced technologies such as Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning, IoT, Edge Computing, and Blockchain with conventional PFC hardware. The proposed system intelligently compensates reactive power and improves power factor in real time by dynamically switching capacitor banks based on load predictions and power quality analysis. At the hardware level, the system utilizes components such as Arduino Uno, ACS712 current sensor, LM358 op-amp, single-channel relays, and ceiling fan capacitors, while more advanced processing is supported through ESP8266/ESP32 modules for connectivity and Jetson Nano or Raspberry Pi for edge AI inference. The ML algorithms, trained using historical load data and power quality parameters, run either on embedded microcontrollers (TinyML) or edge devices for low-latency decision-making. Additionally, a smart capacitor bank is used to provide fine-grained control over reactive power compensation, and system logs are securely recorded through a lightweight blockchain node to ensure transparency in smart grid environments. The integrated ThingsBoard and Node-RED dashboard enables remote monitoring and real-time analytics for system adaptation and performance tracking. Simulation and hardware results demonstrate a significant improvement in power factor correction accuracy and response time compared to conventional fixed or manually switched capacitor systems. The proposed AI-driven model not only adapts to dynamic and nonlinear load conditions but also reduces over- or under-compensation through predictive switching. Comparative analysis confirms enhanced Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) reduction, power factor stabilization, and improved system resilience under varying load profiles. The integration of AI and smart technologies thus marks a promising advancement toward intelligent, autonomous, and transparent power quality enhancement in next-generation smart grids.

title: The 90°C Sauna Paradox of "Human-in-Command": Thermodynamic Delirium, the Biological–Silicon Latency Chasm, and Deterministic Physical-Layer Sovereignty via QFS-zkVM and Sub-100-ns PHOENIX_BRIDGE Interlocks
authors: Yoko(洋子) Hasebe(長谷部)
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Contemporary regulatory frameworks and corporate governance doctrines frequently invoke the slogan "Human-in-Command" (HIC) or "Human-in-the-Loop" (HITL) while leaving human operators embedded inside high-entropy, ultra-low-latency computational environments without deterministic physical-layer actuation. We formalize this structural delusion as the 90°C Sauna Paradox: an operator sitting inside a 90°C (363.15 K) ambient thermal bath—far above mammalian homeothermic equilibrium (T_core ≈ 37.0°C = 310.15 K)—loudly proclaiming "Human in command!" while suffering progressive prefrontal hypoperfusion, hypothalamic thermoregulatory saturation, and an eight-order-of-magnitude latency deficit (τ_bio ~ 10^2–10^3 ms versus autonomous silicon execution τ_AI ~ 10^0–10^2 ns). Using non-equilibrium biothermodynamics, Francisco Varela's neurophenomenology, and Karl Friston's Free Energy Principle, we prove that unassisted vocal or software-mediated assertions of command inside a hyper-entropic bath constitute Zero-Control Acoustic Dissipation (I(Vocal; X_t) = 0). To rescue genuine Human-in-Command from rhetorical theater, we introduce the Deterministic Sauna Inverse-Gating Architecture over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field (F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1). By coupling on-device QFS-zkVM zero-knowledge biometric and metacognitive readiness proofs (π_zk) with PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER and RTO P2.0 sub-100-ns physical-layer interlocks (τ_cutoff = 85 ns), our architecture enforces asymmetric sovereignty: thermally or cognitively compromised operators are cryptographically blocked from relaxing safety invariants (THERMAL_DELIRIUM_LOCK), whereas pre-committed constitutional invariants and emergency physical bus disconnects ("The Hammer") execute deterministically at nanosecond timescales, satisfying SEC Rule 15c3-5 and Delaware Caremark fiduciary duties. title: EdgeNeXt-Attn: A Lightweight Attention-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework for Fire Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
authors: Hikmat Yar; Nehad Ali Shah; Weiwei Jiang; Norah Saleh Alghamdi; Heung Soo Kim
abstract: Wildfires are a major environmental hazard with severe consequences for ecosystems, air quality, infrastructure, and public safety. The rising incidence and severity of wildfire events worldwide have increased the need for reliable early detection and monitoring systems. Remote sensing technologies, such as satellite and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery, along with ground-based Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras, provide valuable geospatial data for large-scale wildfire monitoring. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformer-based architectures, have significantly improved the accuracy of wildfire detection systems. Despite these advances, balancing local feature representation with global contextual modeling remains challenging. CNNs effectively capture local spatial features but have limited receptive fields, whereas Vision Transformers (ViTs) model long-range dependencies but often overlook fine-grained local details and require substantial computational resources. Consequently, accurately detecting small, occluded, and visually ambiguous fire regions remains difficult, particularly for real-time deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address these challenges, this study proposes EdgeNeXt-Attn, an enhanced EdgeNeXt-based framework that effectively integrates local feature learning and global contextual modeling through channel and spatial attention mechanisms. The proposed model improves the detection of small, occluded, and visually ambiguous fire regions while maintaining the computational efficiency required for real-time edge deployment. The proposed framework is evaluated on four multi-platform benchmarks spanning ground-based CCTV (DFAN, Complex-Fire), aerial drone (FLAME), and mixed drone–satellite (ADSF) imagery, achieving 92.09%, 95.16%, 96.65%, and 87.81% accuracy, respectively, and outperforming recent state-of-the-art baselines. With only 5.3M parameters, the model achieves real-time inference at 85.9, 27.3, and 8.4 FPS on GPU, CPU, and Raspberry Pi, respectively. Furthermore, ablation studies and Grad-CAM analysis validate its effectiveness and accurate fire localization. These results demonstrate an accurate and computationally efficient framework for real-time wildfire monitoring using multi-platform remote sensing and ground-based imaging systems.

title: Prototype for Multi-UAV Monitoring–Control System Using WebRTC
authors: Fatih Kiliç; M. A. Hassan; Wolfram Hardt
abstract: Most unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) ground control station (GCS) solutions today are either web-based or native applications, primarily designed to support a single UAV. In this paper, our research aims to provide an open, universal framework intended for rapid prototyping, addressing these objectives by developing a Web Real-Time Communication (WebRTC)-based multi-UAV monitoring and control system for applications such as automated power line inspection (APOLI). The APOLI project focuses on identifying damage and faults in power line insulators through real-time image processing, video streaming, and flight data monitoring. The implementation is divided into three main parts. First, we configure UAVs for hardware-accelerated streaming using the GStreamer framework on the NVIDIA Jetson Nano companion board. Second, we develop the server-side application to receive hardware-encoded video feeds from the UAVs by utilizing a WebRTC media server. Lastly, we develop a web application that facilitates communication between clients and the server, allowing users with different authorization levels to access video feeds and control the UAVs. The system supports three user types: pilot/admin, inspector, and customer. Our research aims to leverage the WebRTC media server framework to develop a web-based GCS solution capable of managing multiple UAVs with low latency. The proposed solution enables real-time video streaming and flight data collection from multiple UAVs to a server, which is displayed in a web application interface hosted on the GCS. This approach ensures efficient inspection for applications like APOLI while prioritizing UAV safety during critical scenarios. Another advantage of the solution is its integration compatibility with platforms such as cloud services and native applications, as well as the modularity of the plugin-based architecture offered by the Janus WebRTC server for future development.

title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG
authors: Mustafa Eriş; Fatma Güneş Eriş; Orhan Yaman
abstract: Recognizing affective states from electroencephalography (EEG) is a core task in affective computing, with applications in mental health monitoring and public safety. Most existing approaches rely on handcrafted features or image-based transformations of EEG, while transformer models capture global context at high computational cost. This study proposes KimiFormer, an end-to-end hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw EEG directly. A hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Stemming (STS) module tokenizes the multichannel signal and learns inter-electrode relationships. Stacked Conformer blocks combine linear and full attention in a 3:1 ratio, reducing computational cost while preserving long-range modeling. The model was evaluated on the public EEG Violence Dataset, recorded with a 14-channel wearable headset from 14 participants viewing violent and neutral videos. Under record-wise leave-one-record-out cross-validation with nested selection of the training hyperparameters, KimiFormer achieved 95.5% accuracy (97.0% under 10-fold cross-validation). On the external DREAMER dataset, its subject-independent performance remained close to chance (balanced accuracy 52.7% for valence and 50.2% for arousal), as did that of two established raw-EEG models. Ablation showed the STS module to be essential (65% accuracy without it). With 3.2 M parameters, 1.51 GFLOPs and an inference latency of 15.64 ms per sample, KimiFormer is suited to real-time, on-device processing of low-channel wearable EEG.

title: Dedicated Edge-AI Single-Board Computer Systems for Ecological Monitoring in Protected Wetlands: Evidence from a Ramsar Site in India
authors: Swapin Vidya
abstract: Abstract Ecological monitoring in protected wetlands increasingly requires continuous, high-resolution data acquisition under conditions of limited power availability and unreliable network connectivity. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has advanced ecological data analysis, many existing approaches rely on cloud-centric architectures that are poorly suited to sensitive and infrastructure-constrained environments. This study evaluates the role of dedicated single-board computer (SBC) systems with on-device AI capabilities for ecological monitoring in protected wetlands.Field deployments were conducted at Sasthamcotta Lake, Kerala, India, a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance and the largest freshwater lake in the state. Two purpose-built, solar-powered edge-AI systems were deployed between August and December 2025 to perform autonomous monitoring under real-world monsoonal conditions. System One focused on real-time validation and anomaly detection of physico-chemical sensor data, including turbidity, pH, and nitrogen levels. System Two integrated periodic biological sampling with AI-assisted image analysis and correlation models to estimate biological indicators, including E. coli presence and Chaoborus spp. (locally referred to as cavaborus larvae), which contribute to the lake’s natural bacterial regulation.The results demonstrate that edge-AI systems achieved high operational reliability (\((>98%)\) uptime), low inference latency (120--180 ms), minimal data loss (\((<1%)\)), and sustained operation using solar power alone. By separating data validation and ecological interpretation across two edge-AI systems, continuous monitoring was maintained without reliance on cloud infrastructure. These findings establish dedicated edge-AI SBC systems as essential infrastructure for ecological research and conservation monitoring in protected and resource-constrained wetland environments.

title: EdgeSafeAI: Real-Time Detection & Classification of Hazardous Events in Public Spaces
authors: Radhika Shinde; Avishkar Bhusare; Akash Gondale; Chaitrali Darekar; Rutuja Hire
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Public safety in smart cities and densely populated environments demands intelligent, low-latency surveillance capable of identifying threats the instant they emerge. Edge-SafeAI proposes a real-time system for detecting and classifying hazardous events in public spaces using edge-based artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision. By leveraging deep learning models optimised for resource-constrained edge devices—including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and lightweight transformer variants—the solution enables efficient monitoring of security threats, accidents, and emergencies with minimal latency. The system processes live video feeds to identify hazards such as violence, fires, and unattended objects, ensuring rapid response while preserving individual privacy through strictly on-device inference. Experimental evaluations demonstrate high accuracy and robustness across diverse real-world scenarios. This paper surveys the state of the art in edge AI, anomaly detection, federated surveillance, and hazard classification, identifies critical research gaps, and positions EdgeSafeAI as a practical contribution toward safer, smarter public infrastructure.

title: Deep Learning in Video and Image Processing
abstract: The Reprint titled Deep Learning in Video and Image Processing Challenges Solutions and Future Directions presents a comprehensive collection of high-quality research addressing the growing demand for intelligent visual systems operating in real time. This Reprint focuses on the practical deployment of deep learning and machine learning techniques for video and image processing on edge devices with limited computational resources. It highlights recent advances that enable efficient model execution under strict constraints related to power consumption memory capacity and processing speed. The Reprint covers a wide range of topics, including lightweight neural network architectures, algorithm optimization, hardwaresoftware co design, and energy-efficient learning models. Emphasis is placed on real-world applications where low latency and on-device intelligence are critical, such as medical imaging, surveillance systems, autonomous driving, smart city monitoring, industrial automation, and wearable health devices. Unlike conventional cloud-based solutions, this Reprint promotes localized data processing to reduce latency enhance privacy and improve system reliability. By bridging theoretical research and practical implementations, the collected works provide valuable insights into scalable and deployable edge intelligence solutions. This Reprint serves as a key reference for researchers, engineers, and practitioners seeking to design robust real-time visual processing systems.

title: Real-Time Streaming H-Pipeline for Sub-Millisecond Sensor-to-LLM Clinical Reasoning: Stages L-A through L-D, an Apple Silicon Empirical Anchor with Analytical Hardware Extrapolation Across Seven Classes, and a 363-Study Validation Campaign at 96.7% SUPPORTED

It contains the complete pre-registration scope document, runner code, summary verdicts, figures, and arXiv-format manuscript for a 363-study empirical validation campaign of the real-time streaming extension of the H-pipeline architecture introduced in Paper 12 and federated in Paper 13. The campaign comprises 363 studies executed in a continuous deterministic protocol (PYTHONHASHSEED=0) across the new streaming Stages L-A through L-D, which together specify the real-time end-to-end streaming H-pipeline operating below standard medical-device latency budgets. The campaign achieves 96.7% SUPPORTED. The v3 manuscript adds an image/video modality extension subsection (§2.5) reflecting Parent L v5 spec sync, including the canonical operating-point table for per-frame feature-embedding mode (W=1.0s, H=0.5s, fs=30Hz, d-axis=5, D-input=768 for ViT-Tiny through ResNet-50). title: A Systematic Literature Review and Conceptual Framework for Consumers of UPI Payment Method
authors: Punam Prakash Patil
abstract: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has fundamentally redefined real-time retail payments, processing billions of transactions monthly and catalyzing the financial inclusion agenda. However, the rapid proliferation of heterogeneous payment instruments linked to UPI—including multi-bank savings accounts, overdraft facilities, on-device wallets (UPI Lite), RuPay credit cards, and pre-sanctioned credit lines—has introduced severe cognitive friction, choice overload, and transactional anxiety for consumers. Concurrently, technical declines, fluctuating core-banking switch latencies, and generic, irrelevant promotional clutter degrade the consumer's perceived experience (CX), dampening long-term continuance intention. While recommender systems (RecSys) have achieved maturity in e-commerce and media streaming, their application within real-time financial execution platforms remains nascent and fragmented. This systematic literature review examines the convergence of recommender systems and consumer perceived experience within the UPI payment ecosystem. Synthesizing over 60 seminal and state-of-the-art studies across technology adoption (TAM, UTAUT2), Information Systems Success (ISSM), Expectation-Confirmation Theory (ECM), behavioral economics (Nudge Theory, Mental Accounting), and algorithmic recommendation (Collaborative Filtering, Context-Aware RecSys, Graph Neural Networks, and Deep Reinforcement Learning), this paper develops an integrative taxonomy of consumer friction points and algorithmic interventions. We examine how real-time, context-aware recommendation engines can dynamically route payment instruments, personalize reward discovery, predict bill settlements, and provide mindful spending nudges without violating low-latency constraints or user data privacy. Furthermore, we evaluate the governance imperatives under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations and Explainable AI (XAI) frameworks. Finally, we formulate a multi-objective architectural blueprint and identify five critical research gaps, establishing an actionable theoretical and computational agenda for doctoral researchers, payment aggregators, and financial system architects.

title: AI-Powered Vehicle Counting and Classification in Smart Cities
authors: Hannah Weber
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science and Engineering
abstract: The rapid growth of urban traffic has outpaced the capabilities of traditional loop sensors and manual surveys, creating an urgent need for scalable, low-latency, and cost-effective traffic intelligence. This manuscript presents an end-to-end, AI-powered system for vehicle counting and classification designed for smart-city deployments. The pipeline integrates single-shot object detection with multi-object tracking to produce de-duplicated counts and fine-grained classes across heterogeneous camera views. The proposed method emphasizes practical constraints: camera placement variability, day–night domain shifts, adverse weather, heavy occlusions, and compute limits on edge devices. We fuse a one-stage detector (for bounding-box localization and coarse class labels) with an appearance-embedding tracker to maintain identities through occlusions and support virtual line-crossing logic that yields robust counts. An optional attribute head refines classes (e.g., car, bus, truck, two-wheeler, auto-rickshaw) using shape priors and aspect ratios. We also introduce normalization techniques (perspective-aware regions of interest, homography-based scale cues, and temporal smoothing) that stabilize predictions under viewpoint changes. Simulation-based evaluations (CARLA + SUMO) emulate dense intersections with configurable lighting and weather, producing 100k labeled frames across five junction archetypes. The system attains high detection accuracy (mAP@0.5 = 0.81), strong tracking (IDF1 = 0.78), and reliable counts (overall MAE = 2.3 vehicles/minute lane-crossing) at 25–30 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson-class edge device via INT8 quantization. A statistical analysis demonstrates consistent performance across classes and time-of-day, with night-time recall improved by temporal voting. The results suggest the approach is deployable at city scale, enabling real-time traffic planning, adaptive signal control, and safety analytics with modest infrastructure upgrades.

title: Android-Based Real-Time Classification of Electric Fire Short-Circuit Traces Using Lightweight Deep Learning Model
authors: Mohammad Hadi Nazari; Junho Bang
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight deep learning framework for classifying electric fire short-circuit traces to enhance safety and fault diagnosis in electrical energy systems. Accurate differentiation between primary (PSCT) and secondary short-circuit traces (SSCT) is essential for identifying failure origins, yet conventional manual inspection is time-consuming and subjective. To address these limitations, we systematically evaluate three lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures MobileNetV2, MobileNetV3, and EfficientNet using transfer learning on a domain-specific image dataset. The models are assessed based on accuracy, loss, precision, recall, and F1-score. Experimental results show that EfficientNet achieves the highest classification accuracy, while MobileNetV3 demonstrates the lowest validation loss and superior generalization stability. Based on a performance–efficiency trade-off analysis, MobileNetV3 is deployed on an Android platform using TensorFlow Lite, enabling real-time, offline, and on-device inference. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first studies to integrate lightweight CNN-based short-circuit trace classification with real-time mobile deployment for on-site energy system fault analysis. By bridging the gap between deep learning and field deployment, the proposed mobile system ensures low-latency execution and provides a rapid, reliable, and portable solution for improving operational safety in electrical fire investigations.

title: Edge AI-Based Smart Healthcare Architecture for Real-Time Arrhythmia Detection Using Lightweight Deep Learning on Wearable Devices Without Cloud IoT
authors: RYO MIRZAVALI ADITYA RYO; Muhammad Raffa Rabbani
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, with cardiac arrhythmias posing a significant challenge because they often occur intermittently and may remain undetected during conventional clinical examinations. Although wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring systems have been increasingly adopted for continuous cardiac surveillance, most existing solutions rely on cloud-based Internet of Things (IoT) architectures, resulting in high communication latency, continuous internet dependency, increased energy consumption, and potential privacy concerns associated with transmitting sensitive medical data. This study proposes an Edge AI-based smart healthcare architecture that enables autonomous real-time arrhythmia detection directly on wearable ECG devices without cloud dependency. The proposed framework employs a lightweight one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) optimized for resource-constrained embedded platforms through model simplification, Global Average Pooling (GAP), and post-training INT8 quantization using TinyML techniques. A single-channel ECG signal is processed locally through an end-to-end pipeline consisting of signal acquisition, noise filtering, heartbeat segmentation, feature extraction, and arrhythmia classification. The model was evaluated using the publicly available MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database and validated through 10-fold cross-validation. Experimental results demonstrate classification accuracy ranging from 94.0% to 97.5%, with 96.8% precision, 96.3% recall, and 96.5% F1-score, while maintaining inference latency below 100 ms and significantly reducing power consumption compared with conventional cloud-based approaches. Local on-device inference also eliminates continuous data transmission, thereby enhancing patient privacy and system reliability. The proposed architecture provides an efficient, low-power, and privacy-preserving solution for wearable cardiac monitoring and demonstrates strong potential for medical-grade wearable devices, remote healthcare services, and next-generation Edge AI-enabled smart healthcare ecosystems

title: Edge-Based Real-Time Condition Monitoring System for Electrical Machines Using Machine Learning
authors: Madhanraj
venue: National Journal of Electrical Electronics and Automation Technologies
abstract: In industrial automation systems, electrical machines are essential resources, failure of which results in expensive downtime, safety and poor efficiency. Predictive maintenance plans have consequently become a necessary tool to detect fault in advance and reduce reliability. Yet, the traditional centralized and cloud-based systems have a critical factor of limitation, such as communication lag, reliance on bandwidth, and cybersecurity, as well as slow decision-making, which limits their use in real-time industrial settings. To solve these issues, the current paper will suggest a condition monitoring framework of electrical machines based on edges, which facilitates fault diagnosis on-device at a significantly low cost in terms of computation. The suggested system combines multi-sensor signal capture, time-frequency systematic preprocessing, and powerful feature extraction, then involving the classical machine learning classifiers, such as, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF), to classify the faults. High diagnostic performance is experimentally proven under varied operating conditions with high accuracy and F1-score and low inference latency to make it be applicable to real-time deployment. Further implementation of edges has confirmed that it will save power consumption and small memory usage, which support the potential of low-cost embedded platforms to implement industrial monitoring. The paper confirms a practical scalable and efficiently energy consuming energy solution to smart condition monitoring in current electrical automation systems using a combination of classical machine learning and effective feature engineering and edge computing has been developed.

title: Hybrid deep learning for smart grid SCADA intrusion detection with mutual information feature selection for smart meter data analysis
authors: Ahnaf Samin; Fariha Zahin; Noholi Islam Duti; Bappaditta Saha Chowdhury; Abdullah Rakib Akand; Mithila Arman; Remon Das; Nkosi Zuberi
abstract: The rapid evolution of smart grid infrastructure has intensified the dependence on SCADA-based supervisory systems for real-time energy management, grid reliability monitoring, and seamless integration of renewable energy sources. However, the growing digitalization of these cyber-physical networks exposes smart meter communication channels and substation control systems to sophisticated cyberattacks that threaten grid stability, energy distribution continuity, and operational safety. This paper proposes a hybrid CNN-Transformer-BiGRU deep learning architecture for intrusion detection in smart grid SCADA networks, designed to jointly address high-dimensional temporal telemetry, severe class imbalance, and industrial measurement noise inherent in smart meter data streams. Unlike prior hybrid CNN-LSTM or CNN-Transformer designs that pair only two complementary inductive biases, the proposed architecture integrates three: (1) two 1D convolutional blocks with Swish activations and batch normalization for local temporal motif extraction; (2) a single Transformer encoder block with eight-head self-attention for global contextual dependency modeling across distributed grid nodes; and (3) a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) layer for bidirectional sequence representation of attack propagation patterns. A reproducible preprocessing pipeline—comprising mutual information-based dimensionality reduction to 60 features, Adaptive Synthetic Minority Oversampling (ADASYN), z-score standardization fitted only on the training partition, and F1-maximizing threshold optimization—ensures class-balanced, leakage-free training. Evaluated on 14,415 held-out samples from the Mississippi State University (MSU) power system benchmark, the proposed model achieves 88% accuracy, macro F1-score of 0.86, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.74, and ROC-AUC of 0.94, outperforming CNN-only, CNN-LSTM, and CNN-Transformer baselines under an identical preprocessing protocol by statistically significant margins (McNemar’s test, \(p < 0.001\) ). Extended ablations isolating mutual information selection, ADASYN oversampling, and threshold tuning quantify the contribution of each preprocessing stage, and five-fold stratified cross-validation reports F1 \(= 0.87 \pm 0.01\) , indicating stable generalization. Operational metrics on the held-out MSU partition—false negative rate of 9%, false alarm rate of 7%, sub-100 ms inference latency on commodity hardware, and a compact 1.5M-parameter footprint—suggest the architecture is a promising candidate for substation-edge deployment, while we explicitly note that field validation on heterogeneous live SCADA traffic remains future work.

title: Nightfall-EX Advanced: An Offline TinyML-Based Portable ECG Monitoring and Emergency Alert System
authors: Anupama Shetter; Sneha M; Shobith. B. R; Prathiba M K
venue: International Conference on Emerging Research in Smart Electronics and Machine Informatics (ECMI)
abstract: Sudden Cardiac Arrest (SCA) remain one of the most critical life-threatening emergencies that demands immediate detection and a rapid medical response. Existing ECG monitoring systems are heavily dependent on smartphones, cloud servers, or uninterrupted internet connectivity, which severely limits their reliability in rural areas and emergency scenarios where network access cannot be guaranteed. This paper present Nightfall-EX Advanced, a fully offline and portable electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring and emergency alert system that incorporates TinyML-based arrhythmia detection directly on an embedded microcontroller. The proposed system integrates a AD8232 ECG front-end for cardiac signal acquisition, a ESP32 microcontroller for on-device signal processing and inference, a SIM800L GSM module for SMS-based emergency communication, and a NEO-7M GPS module for real-time location tracking. ECG signals are acquired, filtered, and classified locally using a lightweight quantized TinyML model trained on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, eliminating any cloud dependency entirely. A manual emergency trigger additionally enables the user to initiates reliable transmission of alert messages embedded with GPS coordinates. Experimental evaluation of the system demonstrated a overall classification accuracy of 93.4 %, with a precision of$\mathbf{9 2. 1 \%}$and recall of$\mathbf{9 1. 3 \%}$for abnormal rhythm detection. Average inference latency was measured between$18-22 ~\text{ms}$, with RAM usage consistently remaining below 120 kB throughout all test conditions. Emergency SMS alerts were successfully delivered within$\mathbf{8}-\mathbf{1 5}$seconds across all trials conducted. These results confirm that the system is well suited for deployment in rural healthcare settings, elderly patient monitoring, and emergency medical response environments where offline and autonomous operation is essential

title: Edge computing and machine learning integration in 6G wireless network
authors: Mohammad Asad Haroon; Manish Madhava Tripathi; Shish Ahmad; Zeeshan Ali Siddiqui; Tamim Ahmad; Deepak Chandra Uprety
abstract: The rise of sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems will bring about a change in connectivity by providing ultra-low latency, massive connectivity, and ultrafast data transfer rates. Achieving these goals will require synthesizing multiple technologies in a way that can push the frontiers of immaturity. The combination of edge computing and machine learning (ML) has now received considerable attention, representing the primary direction for current research and development. Edge computing processes data less at a distance and, therefore, reduces the need for provisioning for centralized cloud computing, latency in processing, and latency to the user. Additionally, edge devices can integrate with ML capabilities and have the potential to execute rapid real-time context-sensitive decisions that, when executed qualitatively, will influence overall network performance and user satisfaction. This chapter focuses upon the synergetic synthesis of the two technologies: ML and edge computing in the environment of 6G wireless communication systems. The emphasis has been on developing opportunities in edge deployment of ML models, providing applications like real-time traffic analysis, predictive module fault identification and risk mitigation, flexible spectrum allocation, and contextual user behavior modeling. In addition, it addresses important problems including the limited computational resources, data privacy requirements, and the difficulty of realizing distributed learning at the edge. The new methods introduced in the chapter include federated learning, reinforcement learning, and TinyML, and their relevance in 6G is studied. The distributed aspects of edge computing along with the learning capabilities associated with ML will be especially beneficial to the design of fully automated, resilient, and efficient 6G infrastructure. This combined approach will enable revolutionary opportunities in the development of new types of innovations including immersive holographic interaction, real-time haptic feedback systems (tactile internet), and fully autonomous services. Finally, the chapter provides a list of the challenges yet to be tackled and suggests potential future research directions to further develop this convergence of paradigmatic shifts.

title: Secure IoT: Behavioral Analysis on a Smart Energy Meter System
authors: Robert-Andrei Manea; Titus Bălan; Alexandru Chiș; Ionuţ-Vlăduţ Dinu
venue: IEEE International Symposium for Design and Technology in Electronic Packaging (SIITME)
abstract: The increasing integration of IoT devices into smart energy systems introduces critical cybersecurity challenges, especially in edge environments with limited resources. This paper presents a novel anomaly detection system implemented directly on a resource-constrained ESP32-S3 microcontroller, enabling real-time, on-device behavioral analysis without relying on external or cloud-based infrastructure. The system uses a compact 1D convolutional neural network deployed with TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (TFLite Micro) to classify anomalies in electrical readings. A custom synthetic dataset was created to simulate realistic operational conditions and behavioral anomalies, including power spikes, flatline patterns, voltage instability, and sensor malfunctions. The microcontroller collects data via a PZEM-004T v3.0 energy sensor and communicates securely over MQTT with TLS to a local broker. A PyQt5 desktop interface enables real-time visualization and alerting. Testing demonstrates reliable detection of anomalous patterns with low latency and without network dependence. By combining embedded machine learning, secure communication, and autonomous design, this work introduces a practical and energy-efficient solution for enhancing security in smart IoT environments. The novelty lies in the successful integration of edge AI for anomaly detection into a fully embedded, low-power system, showing the feasibility of lightweight, local threat awareness in constrained IoT deployments.

title: A Cross-Modal Edge Intelligence Framework for Driver Drowsiness Assessment using Transformer-based Vision and In-Cabin Sensing
authors: Deepak Agarwal; Ganesh Dangwal
venue: International Conference on Expert Clouds and Applications (ICOECA)
abstract: Driver fatigue event, which is a significant cause of road traffic safety accidents with fatal and serious victims, has already taken great number of invaluable lives over past few years; however, most existing detection methods have been confronted with challenges tensing toward singular-modal hint-based manner systems cannot accomplish practical task-worthy performance on real-time instrumented platforms as well as impracticable security assurances on the resource-constraint devices in the direction off-line running. More recently, cloud-based solutions generate obvious time lag and privacy problem, while the already developed method through CNN cannot effectively accommodate illumination variation, occlusion and even temporal driver behavior change. To tackle these problems, in this paper, we propose an Edge-Optimized Multimodal Vision-Transformer (EM-ViT) framework that integrates CNN-based spatial feature extraction with ViT-based temporal attention modeling as well as other in-cabin sensor cues such as eye-aspect ratio and infrared feedback. It is a smart vehicle real-time privacy preserving on-device computation framework. Experimental results on three publicly available datasets (i.e., NTHU-DDD, MRL Eye, UTA-RLDD) demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method under challenging condition of illumination variation, head pose changes and with occlusion and in drivers variability. The proposed EM-ViT always significantly outperforms both the baseline CNN and CNN-LSTM models with up to 99% accuracy, 0.99% F1-score as well as low inference latency (85ms/frame), suggesting a good potential for real-time realization. These results verify poli-fs and transformer-based temporal modeling are effective in enabling multi-modal fusion to be robust and decrease false predictions, suggesting that EM-ViT can be a potential candidate for future intelligent transportation & in-cabin safety use cases.

title: Edge-AI Based Activity Recognition for Elderly Homes
authors: Sadashiv R. Badiger; Aniketanand Sandipkumar; Altaf Shaikh; Anil Brijlal Jaiswal
venue: International Conference on Signal, Systems, and Computing for Next-Gen Automation (ICSSCNA)
abstract: The rapid growth of the aging population has intensified the need for intelligent systems that ensure safety, independence, and timely healthcare support for elderly individuals. This paper presents an integrated framework for activity recognition and assisted monitoring in elderly homes using Edge-AI. The proposed system combines real-time pose estimation, machine learning based activity classification, and IoT-enabled alert mechanisms deployed on a compact edge server. The edge server performs on-device inference using an optimized XGBoost classifier to distinguish normal daily activities from potential fall events. Skeletal key points are extracted using MediaPipe Pose and processed for robust activity recognition. Upon detecting a fall, the system triggers immediate alert notifications to remote caregivers for timely intervention. By operating entirely on edge infrastructure, the proposed system achieves low-latency response, enhanced data privacy, and reduced reliance on cloud connectivity. A lightweight dashboard interface further enables visualization of activity logs for long-term behavioral monitoring and trend analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Edge-AI framework offers a cost-effective, responsive, and scalable solution for intelligent elderly care in resourceconstrained environments.

title: AI-Based Money Recognition Assistant For Blind People
authors: Manjunatha Siddappa; Madhan Gowda Rs; Mohammed Hasham; Naveen Kumar N
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper presents an AI-Based Money Recognition Assistant for Blind People, a low-cost, wearable assistive system designed to enhance the autonomy and safety of visually impaired individuals. The proposed device integrates an ESP32-CAM microcontroller within a spectacle-based form factor, enabling real-time currency denomination recognition and obstacle avoidance. The system utilizes a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) deployed via TensorFlow Lite for on-device currency classification, while an ultrasonic sensor continuously monitors the user's surroundings to detect nearby obstacles. User feedback is provided through a speaker that announces the recognized denomination and a buzzer that issues proximity alerts. By performing all inference locally using Edge AI, the system ensures data privacy, low latency, and complete independence from cloud connectivity. The optimized CNN model, reduced through INT8 post-training quantization, achieves an inference time of approximately 1.2 seconds within the ESP32's limited computational resources. Experimental validation confirms a high recognition accuracy of 93.8% and reliable obstacle detection up to 200 cm, demonstrating the system's effectiveness as a holistic assistive platform for daily financial and navigational tasks.
